**[major] The AST pass replaces the lexical pass for every script it can parse, and it misses sinks the lexical pass found (DOM XSS false negatives)**

When `analyseAST` parses a script, `analyse()` returns early, so the lexical pass no longer runs as a safety net. The AST walker does not visit everything the lexical pass covered. Each of these scripts reports 1 flow at base and 0 at head:
- `window.onhashchange = function(){ document.write(location.hash); };`
- a sink inside a `switch` case
- `function f(){ return eval(location.hash); } f();`

`walkStatement` (`dom_ast.go:198`) has no case for Return, Switch, Labelled, Throw or With statements. `walkAssign` never walks the body of a function literal on the right side of an assignment. The same applies to arrow-function callbacks in `walkCall`.

Either add walker coverage for these constructs, or merge the AST flows with the lexical pass's flows instead of returning early. Either way, add regression tests for these three scripts.

input.body:
**[major] The default `MaxUnitVariantsPerUnit: 16` silently drops active checks on single-URL APIs after 16 distinct requests**

`RequestShapeFingerprint` hashes JSON bodies and most headers byte-exact, so each distinct GraphQL or JSON-RPC operation is its own variant under one per-URL base key (origin + path). After 16 operations, every later one has all its per-URL steps counted as `AlreadyCovered` and never sent. That covers SQLi, reflected XSS, OS command injection, SSTI and Broken access control, not just one check family. The outcome calls this coverage, and no preset, API or UI field can raise the cap.

Either default to 0 (unlimited) and let operators opt in, or exempt bodies that are not form-encoded or not masked from the cap. Also report capped units as not run rather than `AlreadyCovered`.

**[major] BFLA write replay: a 200 refusal envelope is reported as a high/firm finding**

For POST/PUT/PATCH, "B was served" is decided by a 2xx status plus `idorShapeOf(...).same(...)`. That shape compares only JSON key paths and value types, never the values. The write path also drops the stability repeat, which leaves the anonymous control as the only guard. Reproduced:

```
idorShapeOf(`{"success":true,"message":"Settings saved"}`)
  .same(idorShapeOf(`{"success":false,"message":"Admin role required"}`))  // true
```

So an app that refuses non-admins with `200 {"success":false,…}`, and sends anonymous users to a login page, is reported as high/firm Broken access control. The detail text also claims "that write was applied to the target" (line 138), which nothing here verifies. The same happens for HTML apps whose "saved" and "denied" flash messages share one page layout.

For writes, require B's response values to match A's, not just the shape, or better, confirm the write with a follow-up read the way mass assignment does. At minimum, drop "that write was applied" and lower confidence to tentative. A fixture that refuses with a 200 envelope would pin this.

**[major] A read timeout or cancellation partway through the body is now returned as a complete response**

This salvage is too broad. ReadResponseBody wraps any io.ReadFull error in TruncatedBodyError, so a read deadline (`i/o timeout`) or a context cancel that closes the conn mid-body now comes back as a successful response. input.body:
**[major] After one close-delimited response, every later send to that authority silently and permanently gets `Connection: close` written in**

After one frameless HTTP/1 response, the authority stays in `closeDelimitedAuthorities` for the life of the Sender, because nothing ever deletes the key. From then on, every send to it has all its Connection lines replaced with `Connection: close`. The rewrite happens after AuthoriseRaw approved the original bytes, and SendOutcome records no rewrite or Downgrade. So a single HTTP/1.0 error page makes every later hop-by-hop or keep-alive probe to that target go out with a different Connection header from the one the operator wrote, while Repeater, Intruder and the scanner still show the original bytes as sent.

Suggested fix:
- Only add `Connection: close` when the request has no Connection header, or skip the rewrite and just not pool the connection.
- Report any change made to the request in the outcome.
- Clear the mark when ApplyNetwork runs or the pool is flushed.

**[minor] The HTTP/3 pin ignores the upstream proxy policy, the SOCKS carrier and the hostname-resolution override**

`RoundTripH3` builds a bare `http3.Transport` with no Dial hook, and nothing here calls `captureDialIdentity`. QUIC therefore resolves `host` through the system resolver and dials it directly, skipping `dialAddressFor`, the upstream policy and the carrier. With a hosts-style override for a staging IP, or with a carrier set, a send pinned to h3 goes to the public address from the tester's own IP.

There are two options:
- Route the dial through the frozen identity by passing a `Dial` func that uses `id.dialAddr` into `RoundTripH3`.
- Refuse the pin with an error that names the cause when an override, upstream or carrier is active.

No in-tree caller selects `ProtocolPreferenceHTTP3` yet, so this is latent, but `SendRawOutcome` exports it.

input.body:
**[major] A failed HTTP/3 attempt is re-sent over HTTP/1.1 even after QUIC delivered it, so non-idempotent requests are duplicated**

forwardRequest falls back to HTTP/1.1 on any error from forwardH3 when `attempted` is true. But forwardH3's 3s `h3AttemptTimeout` covers the whole exchange inside RoundTripH3: handshake, upload, waiting for the response and `io.ReadAll` of the body. So a request the origin already received and acted on (a POST that takes 4s to answer, or a body stream that breaks partway) is written to the origin a second time over HTTP/1.1, and a non-idempotent request runs twice.

Limit the fallback to failures that happen before any request bytes are sent: dial first under the short timeout, then run the round trip under the normal forward timeout. Treat any failure after the request was sent as final, or at least never replay non-idempotent methods. The note "the endpoint did not answer QUIC" is also wrong in those cases.

input.body:
**[major] The HTTP/3 forward skips the operator's upstream proxy and hostname-resolution override (and `forForwarding`)**

`h3Endpoint` returns `host:port`, and RoundTripH3 dials it over direct UDP to whatever public DNS returns. The HTTP/1.1 leg, by contrast, goes through `s.upstreamDialer()`/the SOCKS carrier and `n.Resolution.DialAddress`. The h3 leg is on by default, so once one retargeted response teaches `Alt-Svc: h3`, later requests leave the configured egress path, or reach production instead of a pinned staging IP. An HTTP or SOCKS upstream cannot carry QUIC, so skip the h3 attempt whenever `s.upstreamPolicy()` is non-empty or `s.carrier()` is set. Also resolve the dial address through `n.Resolution.DialAddress` (keeping SNI = host).

[minor, same spot] The h3 leg also plans the request from raw `requestData` instead of `s.forForwarding(...)`. That drops the Expect stripping and the platform (NTLM/Digest/Basic) credential, so a host that authenticates fine over HTTP/1.1 then gets a 401 over QUIC. h3 responses also never reach `learnFromChallenge` or `altSvc.learn`, so an `Alt-Svc: clear` received over h3 never withdraws the entry.

Add a test that sets an override or upstream policy and asserts that no QUIC dial happens.

**[minor] The HTTP/3 response body is read without the `MaxResponseBodyBytes` cap**

`io.ReadAll(httpResp.Body)` has no size limit, unlike the HTTP/1 reader (`remaining := MaxResponseBodyBytes`) and the h2 leg. On the proxy's Alt-Svc leg, the only bound is the 3s timeout, which limits time, not size: a fast QUIC origin can push hundreds of MB in that window. The sender pin may have no short deadline at all.

Wrap the body in `io.LimitReader(httpResp.Body, MaxResponseBodyBytes+1)`, truncate at the cap, and surface the truncation to the caller the way h2fields does.

**[major] Self-registration skips the per-form cap and dedup, so it creates a new account on every page that carries the form**

The self-registration branch returns before the success-path code that increments `c.formSubmissions[sig]` and records `c.formDestinations[sig]`, and `admitSelfRegistration` updates neither one. input.body:
**[major] The SDL sniff takes over JavaScript bundles that embed `type Query {`, and their routes are no longer read**

An Apollo `gql` template literal has a line that trims to `type Query {`, which matches `looksLikeSDLDocument`. Then `parseGraphQLSDL` fails (e.g. `Unexpected Name "const"`), and `consumeAPIDocument` records SkipAPIUnparsed and returns true. That return comes before the `LooksLikeJavaScript` branch in `perform`, so the bundle's routes are never read. Confirmed: `ParseAPIDocument("application/javascript", "const typeDefs = gql`\n  type Query {...}`;fetch('/api/secret-route')")` returns graphql-sdl plus a failure.

Fix: gate the body-marker form on non-JavaScript content (`!LooksLikeJavaScript(contentType, path)`). Alternatively, when the body sniff is the only signal and the parse fails, return APIDocNone so the body falls through to the next reader. Please add a regression test with a JS bundle that embeds a gql schema.

input.body:
**[major] PaceN takes group slots one at a time, so two concurrent groups can deadlock the whole pool**

PaceN takes its n in-flight slots one at a time, and keeps the ones it already has while it waits for the rest. With cap 4 and two concurrent PaceN(3) calls, each can take 2 slots and then wait on the other forever. Every plain Pace on that pool then hangs too, and only ctx cancellation ends it. ContextPacer is shared across concurrent audits on a named pool, so the race-group paths in `sender/authorised.go` and `authorised_pipeline.go` can reach this.

Make the reservation actually all-or-nothing: serialize group acquisition behind a mutex, or use a weighted semaphore (`x/sync/semaphore` Acquire(ctx, n)) for both Pace and PaceN. Add a test that runs several PaceN calls concurrently against a small cap.

**[minor] Reflection picks the entry file in random map order, so the schema package (and DefaultMessage) is sometimes wrong**

The entry file comes from random map iteration (`for path := range byPath { entryPath = path; break }`). The single "swap to an importer" pass after it does not converge: with a chain a.proto -> b.proto -> c.proto returned in one FileContainingSymbol answer, it can end on b or c depending on map order. SchemaFromFiles takes the package from `files[0]`, so `DefaultMessage()` then returns the dependency's lone message (e.g. "rvc.C" instead of "rva.A"). `api_protobuf_reflect.go` then decodes the body as the wrong type.

Choose the entry deterministically: the first FileDescriptorProto in the response (grpc-go sends the declaring file first), or better, the file that declares `symbol`. Add a 3-file chain test.

**[major] The bench-vulnapp readiness probe polls `/`, but VulnerableApp serves only under /VulnerableApp**

input.body:
**[minor] The signal-escalation killer inherits the slot lock fd, so the slot stays held after the wrapper exits**

The escalation killer `( sleep "$grace"; signal_run KILL ) ... &` is forked while `{lockfd}` holds the slot flock. Unlike the run subshell (`{lockfd}>&-`), it does not close that fd. cleanup() kills only the killer subshell, so its `sleep` child is orphaned and keeps the locked file description: the slot stays held for up to BURPSY_KILL_GRACE seconds after the wrapper exits. Reproduced: after TERM, the wrapper exited 143 immediately, but `flock` on burpsy-heavy.0.lock waited 10s.

Fix: start the killer with `{lockfd}>&-`, or `exec sleep` in a nested subshell and kill the process group.

## Agent review of backlog-b9 at `f9e6739c87d1c0fe1655574295219ad914e97e96`: changes required

This review covers the whole diff against `c42e84a` (483 commits, 848 files; read with `-w`, since much of the UI diff is reformatting). The diff was split into 11 package slices, each reviewed independently. Every finding was then checked by a separate agent asked to refute it against the head code and the base. **37 findings were confirmed (14 major) and 1 was refuted.** The confirmed findings are in the inline comments, except the two below whose lines are outside the diff.

### Major findings
- **Gating / UI:** the client gate resolver can't match `{rest...}` keys, so Sequencer stop/pause/resume fail with a 400 and the capture keeps running (`gated-routes.ts:155` / `api.ts:42`).
- **Scanner false positives at firm confidence:**
  - IDOR `covered=true` without substituting B's credentials (`checks_idor.go:202`)
  - cross-read IDOR with no ownership evidence (`:224`)
  - OAuth redirect_uri canary matching (`checks_oauth.go:193`)
  - state-missing on any 302 (`:219`)
  - BFLA write accepting a 200 refusal envelope (`checks_bfla.go:103`)
- **Scanner false negatives / safety:**
  - the AST DOM pass drops lexical sinks (`dom.go:836`)
  - the variant cap of 16 silently skips active checks on single-URL APIs (`audit.go:1011`)
  - CL.0 is back in the default smuggling run (`checks_smuggling.go:346`)
- **Egress / proxy:**
  - a timed-out or cancelled body read is returned as a complete response (`sender/read.go:82`)
  - a sticky `Connection: close` rewrite is not recorded (`sender.go:1091`)
  - a failed h3 attempt replays non-idempotent requests over h1 (`proxy.go:3600`)
  - h3 bypasses the upstream proxy and the resolution override (`proxy.go:3680`)
- **Other:**
  - self-registration creates an account on every page (`credential_login.go:500`)
  - the SDL sniff swallows JS bundles (`apidoc.go:199`)
  - agent MaxSteps is not enforced within a turn (`run.go:402`)
  - PaceN can deadlock (`limit.go:440`)
  - plugin payload sources (below)
  - the nightly bench readiness probe (`nightly.yml:122`)

### Findings outside the diff
**[major] `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/payload.go:550`: the "plugin" payload source can never be decoded.** `PayloadSource.UnmarshalJSON` has no `case "plugin"`, so any `payload_sources` entry with `"type":"plugin"` fails with `unknown payload source type "plugin"`. The plugin branch in `api_tools.go` (~1380) is therefore unreachable, and every Intruder attack started with a plugin generator returns a 400. Add the case (`var p struct{ Plugin *PluginSource \`json:"plugin"\` }` → `s.Plugin = p.Plugin`). Also make `TestIntruderRunRefusesAPluginPayloadSource*` assert on the `checkPluginPayloadRef` error text: today they pass on the decode error.

**[minor] `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/app.tsx:502`: next/previous-tab chords ignore the saved tab order.** `cycleTool` still walks `TOOLS`, while the strip and View menu render `orderedTools`. Use `orderedTools` here and add it to the useCallback deps.

### CI at this head
- **`beads` fails:** 52 of the 86 newly closed beads have close reasons that don't cite `PR #N (<sha>)` (e.g. `0vzb.4`, `0vzb.8`, `0vzb.9`, `0vzb.24`, `0vzb.25`, `0vzb.28`, `0vzb.50`, `kidb`, `mup0`, `vln1`–`vln3`, `xrq5`). Rewrite them to cite this PR and the landed sha.
- **`review-gate` fails:** risk paths are touched. This review is the verdict, and it is `changes-required`.
- The test shards were still running when the review started.

### Refuted
One finding was refuted: `checks_race.go:131` ("race check replays state-changing requests without CheckAPIWrites").

content.text:
I reviewed all of PR #363 and posted a review on it with **37 confirmed problems (14 major)** and the verdict `agent-review: changes-required`. That's the line `review-gate` reads: it now records "changes required" instead of "no review", and it stays red until a newer approve. I took "post rejects" to mean posting the problems as changes required.

**How the review ran:** 11 reviewers each took one part of the diff (483 commits, 848 files). A separate agent then tried to disprove every finding against the code at head `f9e6739` and at master. 37 findings held up and 1 was thrown out. The posted findings come from those agents, not from me re-checking each one, except the BFLA issue, which I reproduced earlier.

The review is one summary plus 35 inline comments. Two findings sit on lines the PR doesn't change, so they're written into the summary instead.

**The most serious ones:**
- **Broken UI gating:** the console's check for which routes need confirmation can't match the renamed `{rest...}` route keys. Clicking Stop, Pause or Resume in Sequencer gets a 400, and the live capture keeps running against the target.
- **Wrong scanner findings reported as firm:**
  - IDOR is reported when B's credentials were never actually swapped in.
  - IDOR is reported on any resource that only needs a login, with no proof it belongs to A.
  - OAuth redirect_uri and state-missing fire on login bounces and error redirects.
  - The BFLA write replay counts a `200 {"success":false}` refusal as success.
- **Real issues the scanner now misses:**
  - The new AST-based DOM XSS check skips sinks the old pass found.
  - A default cap of 16 request variants per URL silently skips active checks on single-endpoint APIs such as GraphQL.
- **Unsafe probes and sending:**
  - The CL.0 smuggling probe is back in the default run.
  - A failed HTTP/3 attempt is re-sent over HTTP/1.1, so a POST can run twice.
  - HTTP/3 traffic skips the configured upstream proxy and hostname override.
  - A timed-out or cancelled body read now comes back as a complete response.
- **Other bugs:**
  - Crawler self-registration creates an account on every page that has the signup form.
  - The agent's step limit isn't enforced within a single turn.
  - Intruder group pacing (`PaceN`) can deadlock the pool.
  - Plugin payload sources can never be parsed, so those attacks always return a 400.
  - The nightly VulnerableApp benchmark checks the wrong URL for readiness, so it always fails.

**CI at that head**, which I added as a separate PR comment:
- `beads` fails: 52 closed issues don't cite `PR #N (<sha>)` in their close reason.
- `lint` fails with 54 issues; at least some are in files this PR adds.
- `race-web-0` fails: `TestTheCrawlRouteClicksThroughToAScriptRoutedPage` times out.
- `gate` fails right after the test shards.
- Every other test shard, plus `ui`, `uat-cli` and `uat-ui`, passes.

I haven't changed or pushed anything on `backlog-b9`. Should I start fixing, beginning with the beads close reasons and the majors?

[{"id":5658746637,"state":"COMMENTED","body":"## Agent review of backlog-b9 at `f9e6739c87d1c0fe1655574295219ad914e97e96`: changes required

This review covers the whole diff against `c42e84a` (483 commits, 848 files; read with `-w`, since much of the UI diff is reformatting). The diff was split into 11 package slices, each reviewed independently. Every finding was then checked by a separate agent asked to refute it against the head code and the base. **37 findings were confirmed (14 major) and 1 was refuted.** The confirmed findings are in the inline comments, except the two below whose lines are outside the diff.

### Major findings
- **Gating / UI:** the client gate resolver can't match `{rest...}` keys, so Sequencer stop/pause/resume fail with a 400 and the capture keeps running (`gated-routes.ts:155` / `api.ts:42`).
- **Scanner false positives at firm confidence:**
  - IDOR `covered=true` without substituting B's credentials (`checks_idor.go:202`)
  - cross-read IDOR with no ownership evidence (`:224`)
  - OAuth redirect_uri canary matching (`checks_oauth.go:193`)
  - state-missing on any 302 (`:219`)
  - BFLA write accepting a 200 refusal envelope (`checks_bfla.go:103`)
- **Scanner false negatives / safety:**
  - the AST DOM pass drops lexical sinks (`dom.go:836`)
  - the variant cap of 16 silently skips active checks on single-URL APIs (`audit.go:1011`)
  - CL.0 is back in the default smuggling run (`checks_smuggling.go:346`)
- **Egress / proxy:**
  - a timed-out or cancelled body read is returned as a complete response (`sender/read.go:82`)
  - a sticky `Connection: close` rewrite is not recorded (`sender.go:1091`)
  - a failed h3 attempt replays non-idempotent requests over h1 (`proxy.go:3600`)
  - h3 bypasses the upstream proxy and the resolution override (`proxy.go:3680`)
- **Other:**
  - self-registration creates an account on every page (`credential_login.go:500`)
  - the SDL sniff swallows JS bundles (`apidoc.go:199`)
  - agent MaxSteps is not enforced within a turn (`run.go:402`)
  - PaceN can deadlock (`limit.go:440`)
  - plugin payload sources (below)
  - the nightly bench readiness probe (`nightly.yml:122`)

### Findings outside the diff
**[major] `burpsy-go/internal/intruder/payload.go:550`: the "plugin" payload source can never be decoded.** `PayloadSource.UnmarshalJSON` has no `case "plugin"`, so any `payload_sources` entry with `"type":"plugin"` fails with `unknown payload source type "plugin"`. The plugin branch in `api_tools.go` (~1380) is therefore unreachable, and every Intruder attack started with a plugin generator returns a 400. Add the case (`var p struct{ Plugin *PluginSource \`json:"plugin"\` }` → `s.Plugin = p.Plugin`). Also make `TestIntruderRunRefusesAPluginPayloadSource*` assert on the `checkPluginPayloadRef` error text: today they pass on the decode error.

Answers in order.

**2. Corrected count (taking this first, because the summary was wrong).** There are **39 findings: 21 major, 18 minor.** The verified review produced 37 (20 major, 17 minor), and I added two BFLA findings of my own (`checks_bfla.go:103` major, `:11` minor). The "14 major" in the summary was a miscount; the inline labels are correct. 37 of the 39 are inline across 35 comments: `proxy.go:3680` and `nightly.yml:121/122` each pair a major with a minor in one comment. The other two (`intruder/payload.go:550` major, `app.tsx:502` minor) are in the review body, because their lines aren't in the diff. The extra note on `sender/h3.go` is a cross-reference, not a separate finding.

**1. Blocking vs follow-up.**

*Blocks merge: CI.*
- `beads`: 52 close reasons don't cite `PR #N (<sha>)`.
- `lint`: 54 issues (see 4).
- `test (race-web-0)`: `TestTheCrawlRouteClicksThroughToAScriptRoutedPage` times out. The test file predates this branch, so this branch changed what it exercises.
- `review-gate`: clears with a new approve after the fixes.

*Blocks merge: behaviour that is wrong by default, or sends traffic nobody asked for.*
- Sequencer stop/pause/resume get a 400 and the capture keeps running (`gated-routes.ts:155` / `api.ts:42`).
- CL.0 is back in the smuggling run (`checks_smuggling.go:346`).
- A failed h3 attempt replays the request over h1 (`proxy.go:3600`), and h3 bypasses the upstream proxy and the resolution override (`proxy.go:3680`). Both are on the default proxy leg.
- `sender/read.go:82`: a timed-out or cancelled read is returned as a complete response.
- `sender.go:1091`: an unrecorded, sticky `Connection: close` rewrite.
- `agent/run.go:402`: MaxSteps is not enforced inside a turn.
- `credential_login.go:500`: self-registration creates one account per page.
- `intruder/limit.go:440`: PaceN deadlock.
- `intruder/payload.go:550`: plugin payload sources always return 400.
- `audit.go:1011`: the default variant cap silently skips active checks.
- `crawler/apidoc.go:199`: JS bundles lose route discovery.
- `dom.go:836`: the AST pass drops DOM XSS sinks the lexical pass found.

*Owner's call: firm false positives in checks that are off by default.* These are `checks_idor.go:202` and `:224`, `checks_oauth.go:193` and `:219`, and `checks_bfla.go:103`. They only fire when an operator turns on CheckIDOR/CheckIDORTwoIdentity, the OAuth switch, or CheckBFLA+CheckAPIWrites. I'd still fix `checks_idor.go:202` before merge, because it makes every authenticated endpoint a firm IDOR/BFLA once the switch is on. The others can be follow-ups if those switches stay off by default and are labelled experimental.

*Follow-up:* all 18 minors, plus `nightly.yml:122`. That workflow runs nightly, not in PR CI, so it doesn't gate this merge, though the fix is one line.

**3. "review-gate".** This isn't a check run. The workflow `.github/workflows/review-gate.yml` has a job named **`review-gate-run`**, and that job posts a **commit status** with the context **`review-gate`**: it's under the PR's statuses, not its checks (DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md §7). At `f9e6739` it reads `failure — latest verdict: changes-required` (job 121840106006, posted 20:57 UTC).

**4. Lint: all 54 are introduced by this branch, and none were already present.** The job runs `golangci-lint v2.15.0` in *new issues since c42e84a* mode, so issues that already exist on master aren't reported at all. Checking each location against the diff:
- **36 are in files this branch adds**: `authorised_group_test.go` ×8, `extension_services.go` ×4, `checks_sppj.go` ×2, `alpn/fingerprint.go` ×3, `vulnapp_race.go` ×2, `sender/h3.go:44` (G402), and others.
- **16 are on lines this branch added to existing files**: `proxy.go:1876/2002`, `stream_response.go:421`, `grpcproto/schema.go:318/327`, `httputil.go:449`, `ws_live_stress_test.go` ×4 (including :323 inside the new hunk), `listener_test.go:229`, `options_unpack_test.go:358`, `stream_response_test.go:607/623`, `tls_dial.go:145`, `audit_engine.go:849`.
- **2 come from pre-existing code that this branch made fail**: `sender/h2sessions.go:52` and `:160` (SA1019, `http2.ClientConn`). That code was on master, but the branch bumps `golang.org/x/net` v0.57.0 → v0.60.0, which deprecates the type, and it touched those lines.

{"review_threads":[{"id":"PRRT_kwDOToXyo86wcjHl","is_resolved":false,"is_outdated":false,"is_collapsed":false,"comments":[{"body":"**[major] The UI gate mirror can't match `{rest...}` keys, so the console's Sequencer stop/pause/resume now fail with a 400 from the mint**

This PR renamed the generated table's wildcard keys to their mux spelling, for example "/api/sequencer/capture/{rest...}". `manifestPatternFor` (`ui/src/lib/api.ts:42`) did not change and still matches keys by plain segment prefix, so a key containing "{...}" never matches any path. Because of that, "/api/sequencer/capture/stop" (and /pause, /resume) now resolves to the gated exact route "/api/sequencer/capture". The client then mints at /api/sequencer/capture/confirm. But the server's `routeRiskFor` resolves the same URL to "/api/sequencer/capture/{rest...}", so `resolve()` answers 400 "resolves to ..., but this endpoint mints for ...". The stop request is never sent, and the live capture keeps running (`data.workbench.ts:282`, `:292`).

Fix: port `patternMatches`/`literalLen` into `manifestPatternFor`. A trailing `{x...}` acts as its prefix subtree, `{x}` matches one segment, and the key with the most literal text wins. Also add a test that resolves the wildcard paths, e.g. `gatedPatternFor("/api/sequencer/capture/stop")` should be undefined.

`strings.Index(rest, p)` finds the first place the text of the `query=<value>` pair appears in the query string. That is not the position of the pair the loop is on. For `?oldquery={me}&query={me}` it returns 3, inside `oldquery`, so the edit rewrites `oldquery` and still reports success while the real `query` parameter is sent unchanged.

Add up the byte offset as you go over the `&`-split parts (`offset += len(p)+1`) and use that instead of searching again. Please also add a test with a parameter whose name ends in `query` and whose value is the same.

message.content: Do you really need a workflow

content.text:
No, it's not strictly necessary.

**What it buys:** the remaining work splits cleanly. There are eight separate fixes, each in its own files (IDOR, OAuth, CL.0, DOM AST, variant cap, BFLA plus mass-assignment, lint, mixed line endings). There's also a check of about 25 pushed fixes. Running these in parallel worktrees saves wall-clock time, mostly because the scanner test suite alone takes about 8 minutes per run. And the verify step gives the pushed fixes a second reader, which matters because I wrote the findings they answer.

**What it costs:** a lot of tokens. The last review workflow used about 4.3M subagent tokens, and this one will use a similar amount or more. That's up to 22 agents, against this session's guideline of fewer than 10.

**Doing it myself instead:** I'd stop the workflow and work through the eight fixes one after another on `ccr-bca3d2a2-umg0e3`. Each fix would still get a regression test that fails without it, and I'd run the scanner suite once at the end instead of once per fix. I'd check the pushed fixes myself rather than with separate agents. That costs far fewer tokens but takes longer, and you lose the independent check of the pushed fixes.

I'd do it myself, because the fixes are small and well understood. Do you want me to stop the workflow and continue that way? Any agents that have already finished keep their branches, and I'd reuse whatever they produced.

# ci-lint.sh — golangci-lint (v2) and govulncheck for the CI gate (bead burpsy-react-ui-ctdl).
#
#   scripts/ci-lint.sh lint [BASE_REV]   golangci-lint, NEW issues only: findings on lines changed
#                                        since BASE_REV (default HEAD^1). The tree's existing findings
#                                        do not fail the gate; every line a change touches must be clean.
#   scripts/ci-lint.sh vuln              govulncheck over burpsy-go; fails on a reachable vulnerability
#                                        that is not in scripts/ci/govulncheck-baseline.txt.
#   scripts/ci-lint.sh install           install the pinned tools only.
#
# Run from anywhere. Both tools are installed at their pinned versions with `go install` into
# $BURPSY_TOOLS_BIN (default ~/.local/bin) unless that version is already there; the Go module proxy's
# checksum database verifies what is built. Config: scripts/ci/golangci.yml.
set -euo pipefail

GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION=v2.15.0
GOVULNCHECK_VERSION=v1.9.0

root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
bin=${BURPSY_TOOLS_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}
mkdir -p "$bin"
export PATH="$bin:$PATH"
[ -z "${GITHUB_PATH:-}" ] || echo "$bin" >>"$GITHUB_PATH"

install_tools() {
  # Captured, not piped into grep -q: grep exits at its first match, the tool takes SIGPIPE, and
  # under pipefail that made an installed tool look missing.
  local have
  have=$(golangci-lint version 2>/dev/null || true)
  if ! grep -q "version ${GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION#v}" <<<"$have"; then
    echo "installing golangci-lint $GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION"
    GOBIN="$bin" go install "github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/v2/cmd/golangci-lint@$GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION"
  fi
  have=$(govulncheck -version 2>/dev/null || true)
  if ! grep -q "govulncheck@${GOVULNCHECK_VERSION}" <<<"$have"; then
    echo "installing govulncheck $GOVULNCHECK_VERSION"
    GOBIN="$bin" go install "golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@$GOVULNCHECK_VERSION"
  fi
}

cmd=${1:-}
case "$cmd" in
  install) install_tools ;;
  lint)
    install_tools
    base=${2:-HEAD^1}
    if ! git -C "$root" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
      echo "ci-lint: cannot resolve base '$base'; falling back to HEAD^1" >&2
      base=HEAD^1
    fi
    if ! git -C "$root" rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base^{commit}" >/dev/null; then
      echo "ci-lint: no base revision to compare with (is the checkout shallow at depth 1?); refusing to pass" >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "golangci-lint $GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION: new issues since $(git -C "$root" rev-parse --short "$base")"
    cd "$root/burpsy-go"
    golangci-lint run --config "$root/scripts/ci/golangci.yml" --new-from-rev="$base" ./...
    ;;
  vuln)
    install_tools

// outOfTime reports whether the item's static time limit has run out, recording the stop the first
// time it is seen. One clock read per statement: tens of nanoseconds against a pass that costs
// milliseconds, and the price of a limit that is honoured between statements rather than only between
// scripts.
func (e *domEngine) outOfTime() bool {
	if e.budget.Deadline.IsZero() || domNow().Before(e.budget.Deadline) {
		return false
	}
	e.res.Budget.record(DOMStopTime)
	return true
}

func (e *domEngine) analyse(sc domScriptSrc) {

input.body:
Fixes the PR #363 review findings that the fix round at `92e1d43` left open, as listed in the 22:26 status comment on #363. Every commit adds a regression test, and each test was confirmed to fail with its fix reverted.

## Scanner
- **IDOR re-identity** (`checks_idor.go:202`): `covered` is now false when A's cookies ride unchanged, or when a credential header B has no value for stays A's. Before this, A's own replay could become a firm IDOR/BFLA finding.
- **Two-identity cross-read** (`:224`): firm only when an owner-like field names the session's own user id; tentative otherwise. A tentative cross-read no longer stops the one-account probe.
  - The vulnapp cookie fixture therefore now yields **tentative** (test renamed accordingly).
- **BFLA write**: reported only when B's answer equals A's *by value*. The new envelope twin `/api/envelope/admin/settings` (200 `{"updated":false}`) pins this.
  - The unverified "write was applied" claim is gone.
  - The docs now say a captured write can be sent three times. The `ScanConfig` docs no longer say "method escalation".
- **Mass-assignment**: the detail names both canaries, and the evidence quotes the re-read around the persisted one.
- **OAuth**:
  - Location must *be* the variant (absolute URL, same host and path) for a bypass.
  - The state-missing row needs a code or token and no `error=` (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1).
  - `redirect_uri` is located by its decoded name in any spelling. A request without one now returns an error instead of five unchanged resends.
- **CL.0**: out of the plain `CheckRequestSmuggling` run. It runs only under `CheckExtendedActive`, which already admits "Client-side desync". The finding text no longer claims nothing was queued.
- **Variant cap**: `DefaultAuditConfig().MaxUnitVariantsPerUnit` changes from 16 to 0 (unlimited).
- **DOM AST walker** now walks function values assigned to properties, switch cases, return/throw arguments, labelled and `with` statements, and arrow callbacks (block or expression body).

## Lint
- All 19 remaining new-issue findings are cleared (`scripts/ci-lint.sh lint c42e84a` → 0 issues), including `checks_sppj.go` SA9003/S1039.
- The `gosec` warnings on the deliberately vulnerable JSON fixtures and the issue-name constant are suppressed, each with its reason. Fixture behaviour is unchanged.

## UI
- Pretty view of HTML/XML under a CRLF head: the breaks it inserts between tags now use CRLF, so the editor shows separate lines. A text node's own newlines are left as they are.

## Still open
- **Raw display of a mixed-ending message** (CRLF head, LF body): the LF body still shows as one line. Fixing that needs a position map between CodeMirror lines and the real bytes, which is a design change; it is not in this PR.
- **Production plugin Grants wiring**: untouched here.
- **Pushed fixes not re-verified**: this PR does not independently re-check the fixes that were pushed in `f9e6739..92e1d43`.

## Validation
- `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean. `gofmt` is clean on changed files; `internal/netauth/ntlm_test.go` is already unformatted at `92e1d43`.
- `scripts/ci-lint.sh lint c42e84a` → 0 issues.
- T1 on `scripts/affected-go-tests.sh 92e1d43`:
  - `cmd/burpsy`, `browser`, `extension`, `mcp`, `persist`, `proxy`: ok.
  - `crawler`, `scanner`, `web`: their failures were all missing tools (no Chrome on PATH, no ffuf). With Chromium on PATH, the failing tests pass, including `TestTheScannerDetectsWhatTheTargetDeclaresItIsVulnerableTo` (the full corpus) and `TestTheCrawlRouteClicksThroughToAScriptRoutedPage`.
  - The two ffuf tests were not run.
- `bun run check` passes (UI).

content.text:
I fixed the review findings the last round left open and opened draft **PR #364** into `backlog-b9`: https://github.com/Chaim12345/burpsy/pull/364. It's 8 commits on `ccr-bca3d2a2-umg0e3`. I stopped the multi-agent workflow before it produced anything and did all of this myself to save tokens. So the earlier "review the fixes" part was cut short: I haven't re-checked the fixes already pushed to `backlog-b9` (`f9e6739..92e1d43`).

**What I fixed:**
- **Lint:** all 19 remaining issues; the repo's lint script now reports 0.
- **IDOR:**
  - A replay is no longer counted as identity B when A's cookie or an unfilled credential header was left in place.
  - The two-identity check is only "firm" when the response names A's own user id; otherwise it's "tentative". With the existing cookie-based test fixture it now reports tentative, so I renamed that test.
- **BFLA write:** B's answer must match the admin's by value, not just by shape. A new test fixture refuses with a 200 `{"updated":false}` response to pin this, and the docs are corrected.
- **Mass-assignment:** the finding now names both canaries, and the evidence quotes the re-read body that holds the persisted value.
- **OAuth:**
  - A bypass counts only when the redirect actually goes to the manipulated URI.
  - The missing-state check needs a real grant and no `error=`.
  - `redirect_uri` is found however it's encoded; if it can't be found, the check errors instead of silently re-sending the original request.

content.text:
Yes, theirs is better, and theirs is what's on `backlog-b9` now. I checked each of the five files:

| File | Mine | Theirs |
|---|---|---|
| `listener_test.go` | `_ = conn.SetReadDeadline(...)` | fails the test (`t.Fatalf`) if the deadline can't be set |
| `session_gate_legs_test.go` | `_ = origin.Serve(oln)` | reports any error except the expected shutdown ones (`ErrServerClosed`, `net.ErrClosed`) |
| `stream_response_test.go` | discarded both errors | origin goroutine logs a failed write and returns; the deadline failure fails the test |
| `tls_truncation_test.go` | `_, _ = bw.WriteString(body)` | logs a failed write and returns |
| `ws_live_stress_test.go` | discarded all three | deadline failures fail the test; the feed goroutine logs and returns |

Mine silenced the linter by throwing the errors away. Theirs checks them, so a broken test setup fails loudly instead of showing up later as a confusing timeout.

I also checked the usual risk with that pattern, calling `t.Fatal` from a goroutine the test spawned. Every `t.Fatal`/`t.Fatalf` they added runs on the test's own goroutine. Inside spawned goroutines they use `t.Logf` plus `return`, or `t.Errorf` in the one case where only the shutdown errors are expected.

One thing mine covered that theirs doesn't: a second unchecked `f.client.Write` in `ws_live_stress_test.go` around line 94. It was already there before this branch, so the lint gate doesn't flag it, and it doesn't affect anything now.

On the merged tree, lint reports 0 issues and `internal/proxy` passes, so nothing needs changing.

If you mean PR #364: it's already merged into `backlog-b9` (`90c3a04`). If you mean PR #363 into master, I haven't merged it, because three checks are red at its head `90c3a04`:

1. **`ui` fails because of my UI change.** The committed `dist/app.js` no longer matches a fresh `bun run build` (bun 1.4.2), since my `message.ts` change needs a rebuild. Per DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS §5 the lead does that rebuild once per round. This container has bun 1.4.4, so I'd install 1.4.2, rebuild, and send the bundle through a PR into `backlog-b9` like #364.
2. **`review-gate` reads "changes-required".** My own `changes-required` verdict is still the latest. The process needs a fresh reviewer, not the author, to post `agent-review: approve <sha>` for this head. I wrote both the findings and the fixes, so approving it myself would defeat the gate.
3. **GitGuardian flags 3 "Username Password" hits** in `crawler/credential_isolation_test.go` and `credential_login_test.go`. They look like test fixtures, but someone should mark them in the GitGuardian dashboard rather than ignore them.

Everything else is green: `gate`, all test shards, `lint`, `beads`, `uat-cli` and `uat-ui`.

Merging #363 puts 483 commits and 848 files on master, which is hard to undo, so I'd rather not do it past red checks. I'd do the bundle rebuild now, then you get the independent approve (I can start a fresh reviewer agent for that if you want), then merge. Should I start with the rebuild? If you want #363 merged now despite the red checks, say so and I will.

10 findings, most severe first:

1. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/checks_bfla.go:110`: bflaSameValues makes a write BFLA require B's answer to equal A's baseline leaf for leaf, so any write whose answer carries a per-call value (created id, timestamp, updated_by, version, request id) is never reported.

   Failure scenario: A low-privilege user can POST /api/admin/users. A's baseline returns {"id":41,"created_at":"...:01"} and B's replay returns {"id":42,"created_at":"...:02"}. Same shape, different values, so the check returns nil and silently drops a real privilege-escalation finding. Only stable leaves (or the status/flag leaves) should be compared.

2. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/checks_idor.go:196`: idorReidentity counts the replay as B's as soon as ANY cookie name is shared, even when A's session cookie rides through unchanged; the fix covers only the no-shared-name case.

   Failure scenario: A sends `Cookie: sessionid=A; csrftoken=x` and B's CookieHeader is `csrftoken=y; session=B`. Only csrftoken is replaced, so covered=true and the request is still authenticated as A. The cross-read / BFLA replay then 'succeeds' as A and reports broken access control (tentative IDOR, or a BFLA finding) for what is really A's own access.

3. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/checks_bfla.go:119`: The anonymous control for writes still compares by shape only, while this PR established that a 200 refusal envelope has the success shape. A vulnerable endpoint that refuses anonymous callers with that envelope is suppressed.

   Failure scenario: The endpoint answers anonymous POSTs with 200 {"updated":false,"setting":"banner"} and B (non-admin) with 200 {"updated":true,...}, the real write. B passes bflaSameValues, but nr is 2xx with the same shape, so the check returns nil and the BFLA is missed. The control should use bflaSameValues for writes too.

4. `burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/message.ts:421`: prettyMarkup inserts `sep` only between directly adjacent tags; existing newlines are split on \n, trimmed (dropping \r) and re-joined with bare \n. A CRLF HTML body with line breaks between tags still renders as one line, and text-node CRLFs are rewritten despite the doc comment.

   Failure scenario: Response with CRLF head and body `<html>\r\n<head>\r\n<title>x</title>`: no `><` adjacency, so every line is joined with `\n`. The editor splits on CRLF and shows the whole body on one line, the exact bug PR 363's review asked to fix. A text node `a\r\nb` also comes back as `a\nb`, contradicting 'a newline already inside the body stays exactly as it was'.

5. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/checks_idor.go:1262`: idorOwnedBySession treats the object's own primary key (`id`, `pk`, `uuid`) as an owner field, so an object whose id merely equals the user's numeric id is upgraded to firm.

   Failure scenario: JWT sub=1 and GET /api/orders/1 returns {"id":1,"total":5} for a shared, login-only record. `$.id`="1" matches the session, so the cross-read becomes firm, and the detail claims the order 'belongs to the first identity'. That is the exact false positive the tentative downgrade was meant to stop. A top-level `id` should be excluded; only owner-named fields (user_id, owner, sub) should count.

6. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/dom_ast.go:405`: walkAssign now walks every assigned handler or arrow body in a fresh child scope on each propagation round. Any local tainted binding inside the handler is therefore 'newly bound' every round, so the fixpoint never reaches added==0.

   Failure scenario: `window.onhashchange = function(){ var h = location.hash; ... }`: each round creates a new domASTScope and bind('h') returns true, so added>0 forever. Propagation burns all MaxPropagationRounds (and the statement budget), then records DOMStopPropagationRounds, a false 'chain continues past here' budget stop on ordinary pages. It also starves the sink pass of budget.

7. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/checks_smuggling_cl0.go:112`: This PR gates CL.0 in the smuggling row because the probe can queue a response on a SHARED back-end connection, but checkClientSideDesync runs the same smuggledPrefixProbe and still says 'The proof never leaves the scanner's connection'.

   Failure scenario: With extended-active on, both rows fire the same probe per host, so the risky prefix is sent twice. An operator reading the Client-side desync row's code or comments is told it is harmless, contradicting the new ScanConfig documentation and smuggling detail text. The comment should be corrected, and the result shared or deduplicated between the two rows.

8. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/checks_idor.go:1249`: idorOwnedBySession duplicates idorOwnerBinding's sorted-key loop and owner-name predicate almost verbatim instead of sharing it.

   Failure scenario: Two copies of the owner-field rule (`idorIDName(last) || owner || sub`, the last-segment slicing) must be kept in sync. A fix to one, such as excluding the primary-key `id` above, silently misses the other. idorOwnerBinding could be built on idorOwnedBySession plus the swapped-object check.

9. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/checks_oauth.go:234`: oauthLocationTargets requires an exact path match, so a registered redirect_uri with an empty path never matches the server's normalized Location path '/'.

   Failure scenario: registered=https://app.example gives the subdomain variant https://app.example.canary with Path "". A vulnerable server redirects to https://app.example.canary/?code=x with Path "/". The paths are not equal, so a real redirect_uri bypass is reported as validated. Paths should be normalized ("" == "/").

10. `burpsy-go/internal/scanner/audit_engine.go:849`: The uint32→uint64 widening in unitVariantCapped is a no-op change: len(set) cannot approach 2^32 here, and the comparison was already correct.

    Failure scenario: Adds noise to a hot-path comparison with no behavioral effect. Keep `uint32(len(set)) >= capN`, or compare as int, instead of double casts that suggest an overflow bug that does not exist.</local-command-stdout>

scanner: second-pass fixes from the PR #364 code review

- BFLA write: the value match leaves out per-call values (a created id, a timestamp, a request
  id), so a real write that answers with one is no longer dropped; booleans and status words must
  still match. The anonymous control is judged by value for a write too, so an anonymous 200
  refusal envelope no longer hides a finding (/api/anon-envelope/admin/settings pins it).
- IDOR re-identity: every cookie name in B's set must be replaced in A's header; one shared name
  (csrftoken) no longer counts while A's session cookie rides under another name.
- Ownership evidence: an object's own primary key ($.id, order.id) and another object's id
  (product_id) are no longer owner fields; only person-named ids, owner, sub and uid are. The
  cross-read and the one-account binding share the rule (idorOwnerKey).
- DOM AST: one child scope per function value and call site across propagation rounds, so a
  handler with its own locals reaches a fixpoint instead of spending every round.
- CL.0: the smuggling row and "Client-side desync" share one probe per endpoint, and the
  Client-side desync comment no longer says the proof never leaves the scanner's connection.

## ctdl [open] Add golangci-lint (v2) and govulncheck to CI
  D: CI runs only gofmt and go vet. Add golangci-lint with a small bug-finding set (staticcheck, errcheck, gosec, bodyclose, ineffassign; misspell) and govulncheck — the binary links a large transitive tree via gitleaks (viper, cobra, sprig, mholt/archives, wazero, go-re2). Fix or annotate existing findings first so the gate starts green. Doc §2.  INTEG
  N: 

## xnet2h [open] P1: pin golang.org/x/net off the self-deadlocking http2 wrapper (v0.57.0) + upst
  D: W11 root-caused the evmi CI red: x/net v0.57.0 http2 wrapper roundTrip holds cc.mu while calling cc.Reserve, whose state hook re-locks cc.mu - same-goroutine self-deadlock, wedged forever (mutex waits ignore context, no timeout fires). Frequency scales with concurrent h2 sends (~1/run at -parallel 12, green at 4 by luck). Fix: pin x/net to a versio
  N: 

## uat1 [open] UAT: CLI end-to-end step in CI
  D: User directive (2026-10-25): add a UAT testing step to the pipeline covering the CLI. Build the burpsy CLI binary in CI and exercise real user flows, not unit suites: start the proxy, drive traffic through it, run a scan against a fixture target, verify findings and exit codes. Lane: W5 ci-core owns the pipeline step.  NOTE 2026-10-26 (test-only me
  N: 

## uat2 [open] UAT: browser UI smoke in CI
  D: User directive (2026-10-25): add a UAT testing step covering the browser UI. Drive the real console in a browser (Playwright or equivalent) against a dev server: load the console, send a Repeater request, view the exchange in history. Split ownership: W2 web-ui builds the harness under ui/, W5 ci-core wires it into the pipeline. Note CI Chrome flak
  N: 

## sppjmk [open] vulnapp_sppj.go:91 makeslice on ContentLength == -1
  D: Independent pre-existing defect found during W11's evmi investigation: vulnapp_sppj.go:91 calls makeslice with ContentLength == -1 (unknown length). Guard the -1 case. 2026-10-26 CI evidence (integrator): the panic 'http: panic serving ... runtime error: makeslice: len out of range' at vulnapp.sppjJSON (vulnapp_sppj.go:91) is printed in the logs of
  N: 

## crlfp [open] CRLF check: possible false positives on vulnapp safe twins (/crlf/safe/*)
  D: j1mk.15's first live parity run (crlfuzz v1.4.1 vs burpsy, demo-target fixtures): burpsy reported header injection on ALL THREE safe twins (/crlf/safe/r/home, /safe/ref, /safe/unicode), contradicting the vulnapp safe-twin contract. crlfuzz P/R 1.0/0.333 on the same rows; burpsy 0.167/0.333. Verify against the fixtures whether these are genuine scan
  N: 

## 2o0c [open] CI: Chrome fails to start in some test shards — confirm the cause from the warm-
  D: Shards on GitHub runners failed with 'websocket url timeout reached' (recorded-login test in web/race-web-0 at 20s; every DOM row in scanner-detect at 30s). Same runner image and Chromium 154 as green runs; passes locally. #353 (merged) warms Chrome before the tests with domexec's flags and prints Chrome's stderr tail on failure. When Actions runs 
  N: 

## r78q [in_progress] scanner: passive check flags a response reflecting a normalized form of an input
  D: Optional half of burpsy-react-ui-d617 (the normalize payload processor shipped). A passive/active check that flags a response reflecting a NORMALIZED form of an input different from what was sent — evidence the server normalizes after validating, the tell for the Unicode-normalization bypass class. Reuse internal/intruder/normalize.go's forms: send
  N:  ASCII probe may shift the big test's other transformation detections; needs validation against runtime_coverage_test), or skip the fullwidth pass on insertion points that write stored state. Must map to Burp catalog issue 'Suspicious input transformation (reflected)' (TypeIndex present; native registry requires one descriptor per catalog issue, so ENHANCE that check, do not add a second). Reusable: toFullwidth(s) maps ASCII printable -> +0xFEE0.

## wflj [in_progress] scanner: cannot test an MCP server as a target — enumerate and probe its tools/r
  D: ## Claim  burpsy cannot test an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server as a target. As AI agents adopt MCP, the servers they connect to become an attack surface — over-broad tools, injectable prompts/resources, tools that reach internal services — and ZAP added first-class MCP-target scanning in 2026. burpsy has no notion of MCP as a target.  ## Scope
  N: -target scanning IS in burpsy's scope. Extensive online research dispatched (threat catalogue, protocol/transports/auth, existing scanners, standards mapping). Uncommitted WIP exists in internal/mcpscan + web/api_mcpscan.go (builds, tests pass, not wired to routes). 2026-10-09: a native scanner port exists on branch beads/f-mcpscan (cdd8230b), held as reference per the user's decision of 2026-10-09; wflj follows the Sept 27 opt-in mcprobe design.

## vnlh [open] Route with Go 1.22 method/path patterns and declare each route once
  D: internal/web has 218 manual r.Method checks, 194 StatusMethodNotAllowed, 27 TrimPrefix ID parses and 0 PathValue; the same routes are declared in server.go, route_manifest.go, route_schemas.go and mcp/groups.go (drift bugs u9t6, s9ma; method bug 0gg5). Register "POST /api/x/{id}" patterns and generate the manifest/schemas/MCP groups from one table.
  N: 

## h2sess-stamp [open] H2Sessions keys carry no route/cert stamp (h2sessions.go)
  D: W3 source finding at ce9668d5, not runtime-verified. H2Sessions keys carry no route or client-cert stamp, so a session may outlive a route or cert change. Outside o388's HTTP/1 scope.  Narrow fix landed (H2 stack ea418bdc, which contains o388 27d64139): mid-exchange stamping for H2 sessions. CI 40281581790 green at ea418bdc. This bead stays OPEN: t
  N:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""beads-lint.py — check .beads/issues.jsonl against the closure rule in docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md.

    python3 -I scripts/beads-lint.py --base BASE [--head HEAD] [--jsonl PATH]

The rule exists because "closed" stopped meaning "landed": beads were closed for work that never
reached master (wtm2, qpfy, tni8, lxqq), and only about a quarter of closures named a commit at all.
So a closure must now point at the commit that did the work, and that commit must be in the history
being merged. Existing closures are grandfathered: only what changed between BASE and the file
checked here is judged.

Checks, each reported with the bead id it concerns:
  1. every line is a JSON object with a string "id", no blank lines, the file ends in a newline;
  2. ids are unique;
  3. no bead present at BASE has disappeared (an export that loses issues is how a merge driver once
     wiped the 264-issue tracker — see .gitattributes);
  4. every bead NEWLY closed (open at BASE, or absent there and added closed, or closed at BASE with
     a changed close_reason) has a close_reason that either
       a. cites `PR #N (<sha>)` or `PR #N (merge <sha>)` — the form both the close script and the
          existing closures use — and every cited sha is a commit that is an ancestor of HEAD; or
          starts with `MERGED via integrator` and names the landed commit(s) in its opening clause,
          only as "(<sha>)", "at <sha>" or "(<sha>+<sha>)", each an ancestor of HEAD. Shas are lowercase hex.
          A "+" after a citation that does not continue it as "+<sha>" (spaces around it, a word after
          it) is rejected as malformed. A sha written in prose after the citation, as in
          "(<sha>, W3 tip <sha>)", is NOT read or checked: only the cited position is. This is for
          merges the integrator made without a PR; no PR number is invented and a closure with no sha
          is still rejected; or
       b. says it fixed nothing and names why: starts with "Duplicate of <id>" / "Superseded by
          <id>" (an id in this file), or with "WONTFIX", "Won't fix", "INVALID" or "Not a defect".
          Those land no code, so there is no commit to cite; they are not an escape hatch for work
          that was done (a reviewer reads them in the diff); or
       c. the bead is an epic with at least one child (a parent-child dependency on it), and every
          child is closed in this file — the children carry the commits.

BASE: in CI, HEAD^1 — for a pull request the checkout is GitHub's merge commit, whose first parent
is the base branch it merges into; for a push to master it is the previous tip. Needs full history
(actions/checkout fetch-depth: 0). In a shallow clone a commit older than the clone's history cannot be
found and is reported as missing, with a warning that the clone is shallow.

Exit status: 0 clean, 1 rule violations, 2 usage or environment error.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

JSONL = ".beads/issues.jsonl"
FIX_RX = re.compile(r"PR #(\d+) \((?:merge )?([0-9a-f]{7,40})\)")
# "MERGED via integrator (<sha>)", "... at <sha>", "... fast-track (<sha>+<sha>)": the form closures use when a
# change lands by the integrator's own merge and no PR number exists (none may be invented). Only the
# opening clause is read. A sha counts only in one of those positions: right after "(" or "at ", with
# further shas joined by "+". A hex-looking word elsewhere in the clause is not a citation.
MERGED_RX = re.compile(r"^MERGED via integrator\b[^.:;\n]{0,80}")
_SHA = r"[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b"
SHA_RX = re.compile(r"(?:\(|\bat\s+)(" + _SHA + r"(?:\+" + _SHA + r")*)")

## Code
- **`324fa6f` scanner:** fixes the 9 findings from the code review of the #364 merge.
  - **BFLA write match:** per-call values (created id, timestamp, request id) are left out of the comparison, and the anonymous control is judged by value. A new fixture, `/api/anon-envelope/admin/settings`, pins this.
  - **IDOR coverage:** every cookie name in B's set must be replaced before the replay counts as B's.
  - **Ownership:** an object's own primary key and other objects' ids no longer count as owner evidence. The cross-read and the one-account binding now share one rule, `idorOwnerKey`.
  - **DOM AST:** each function value and call site keeps one child scope across rounds, so handlers with locals reach a fixpoint instead of spending every round.
  - **CL.0:** one probe per endpoint, shared by the smuggling row and "Client-side desync". The comment that claimed the probe never leaves the scanner's connection is corrected.
  - **OAuth:** an empty path and `/` count as the same URL.
- **`92db77f` ui:** Pretty markup now also breaks between tags the body already separated with CRLF, and keeps a text node's own CRLF.
- **`1b95b32`:** bundle rebuilt with bun 1.4.2.
- **`273f76a` vulnapp (sppjmk):** the sppj profile handler read its body into a buffer sized by `ContentLength`, which is -1 for a chunked body, so it panicked. It now reads the whole body, capped.

## 6. PRs and merging

1. The agent commits on its branch with substantive messages and a `Bead: <id>` trailer for each
   bead the branch completes (`Bead: ar8v` or the full id; several ids may share a trailer). A bead
   the branch only advances gets no trailer.
2. The lead opens the item's PR **against the round branch** with the agent's report as the body
   (what changed, what was verified, what was not). Risk-class items (§7) get their reviewer now.
   CI does not run on these PRs (workflows run only for PRs into master); T1 and T2 cover them.
3. After T2 the lead merges the item into the round branch:

       git merge --no-ff -m "Merge PR #<N>: <PR title>" <item branch>

   and pushes; GitHub marks the PR merged once its head is in the round branch. The `Merge PR #N:`
   subject is what `scripts/beads-close-merged.py` reads the PR number from (a merge made with
   GitHub's merge button is also understood).
4. The lead rebuilds the bundle, runs the close script (§9), commits both, opens the **round PR to
   master** listing the item PRs and beads, and sets `gh pr merge --auto --merge` (needs "Allow
   auto-merge" in the repository settings).
5. Red T3: fix forward on the round branch, or `git revert -m 1` the offending item merge, take its
   beads out of the closure commit, and say so in the round PR.

Hotfixes: a single PR to master, same required checks, same closure rule.
Merge commits only — no squash, no rebase — so every closure sha stays in master's history.

## 7. Review

content.text:
I didn't merge #363. The independent reviewer posted **`agent-review: changes-required`** at `1253ce3` (06:28 today), and `review-gate` is red with that verdict. Merging now would put two defects it found on master.

Everything else is green at that head: every test shard, `lint`, `ui`, `beads`, `uat-cli` and `uat-ui`. The only other red check is GitGuardian, which needs its incident marked in the dashboard.

The reviewer confirmed all four earlier risk-path findings are resolved, then found two new blocking defects:

1. **A data race that can crash the process** (`sender/sender.go:453`). `ApplyNetwork` resets the close-delimited map with `= sync.Map{}` while in-flight sends read and write it. Saving network settings mid-send can end in a fatal `sync: unlock of unlocked mutex`. They reproduced it under `-race`. The fix is one line: `s.closeDelimitedAuthorities.Clear()`.
2. **`SendOutcome.Note` is written but never read.** The note meant to record "`Connection: close` added" or "h3 body cut at the cap" never reaches the stored Repeater exchange. A request that was modified, or a truncated response, is stored looking untouched. The fix is to merge `outcome.Note` into the exchange's notes in `recordRepeaterExchange`, with a test that the note lands on the stored exchange.

Two non-blocking points:
- `ui/src/lib/api.ts` (the client gated-route resolver) should be added to the risk list in `scripts/review-gate.sh`.
- The HTTP/3 dial ignores the IPv4/IPv6 preference.

Fixing both defects would take a PR into `backlog-b9` as before. Because `sender/` is a risk path, that push invalidates the verdict, so #363 then needs another independent review at the new head before it can merge. Should I go ahead with the fixes?

input.title: Hotfix: close-delimited marks race in ApplyNetwork; Repeater rows record what the sender changed
input.body:
Hotfix to master for the two blocking defects from the independent review of PR #363 (comment 6435363644). They were deferred when #363 was merged.

## Fixes
1. **Data race (`sender/sender.go:453`).** `ApplyNetwork` reset `closeDelimitedAuthorities` with `= sync.Map{}` under `s.mu`. In-flight sends `Load`/`Store` that map without `s.mu`, so a network-settings save during a send could hit a fatal `sync: unlock of unlocked mutex`. The map is now cleared in place with `Clear()`.
   - New test `TestApplyNetworkClearsCloseDelimitedMarksWithoutRacingSends` is race-clean with the fix. With the old reassignment it reports `DATA RACE` under `-race`.
2. **`SendOutcome.Note` never reached the stored exchange.** The note says when the sender added `Connection: close` or cut an h3 body at the cap. Without it on the stored Repeater exchange, a modified request or a truncated response looked untouched. Now:
   - the single send (`api_tools.go`) and the synchronized group send (`api_repeater_group.go`) append it to the exchange note, after the tab's note, as `[burpsy] …`;
   - a failed send carries it into the tool log's error text.
   - New test `TestARepeaterSendRecordsWhatTheSenderChanged`: a close-delimited origin, two real `/api/repeater/send` calls; the second stored row's note says `Connection: close` was added. It fails with the wiring removed.

## From the review's non-blocking points
- `scripts/review-gate.sh` now lists `ui/src/lib/api.ts`, the client gated-route resolver, as a risk path.
- **Not changed: the h3 address-family point.** The proxy's own `NetworkSettings` carries only `Resolution`, `Continue` and the Alt-Svc switch, with no family preference. Its TCP legs dial with the same `Resolution.DialAddress` the h3 leg uses, so the legs are consistent.

## Validation
- `gofmt` and `go vet` clean. `scripts/ci-lint.sh lint origin/master` reports 0 issues.
- `go test ./internal/sender ./internal/web` passes. The two `web` tests that need Chromium or ffuf pass with Chromium on PATH; the ffuf test runs with `BURPSY_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EXTSCAN=1`.
- `-race` on the two new tests passes.

## Review
This touches risk paths (`internal/sender/`, `scripts/review-gate.sh`), so it needs an independent `agent-review` verdict at its head (DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS §7).

content.content:
## 4xqt3-unmount-setbusy [open P3] 4xqt.3 P3: unmount setBusy on a stale GraphQL editor instance
From the 4xqt.3 review: a setBusy call can land on an unmounted or stale editor instance. Guard it and pin it.

## 4xqt3-speculative-render-discard [open P3] 4xqt.3 P3: speculative-render conservative discard
From the 4xqt.3 review: the speculative-render path discards conservatively. Pin the intended contract with a test.

## 4xqt3-binding-tests [open P3] 4xqt.3 P3: competing-finally and same-tick-abort binding tests
From the 4xqt.3 review: add binding tests for competing finally blocks and same-tick abort in the editor busy-reset guard.

## credfx [open P3] crawler crediso residuals: pause re-check on frontier-drain path, login-form-ignored metric, authChallengedSeen doc
Filed at crediso close (integrator, 2026-10-25). (a) Narrow ordering: a retry that BOTH enqueues links AND trips pause policy can take one more visit before the normal post-visit policy check - the frontier-drain continue runs ahead of it. Fix: re-check pause/stop policy before each dequeued frontier visit; test the combined shape (the committed test binds timeout-only). Bounded: the extra visit stays in the CURRENT credential session, no isolation crossing. (b) login-form-ignored counts any later form encounter, not distinct auth methods - metric fidelity. (c) authChallengedSeen doc says 'every URL admitted' but direct-perform paths bypass enqueue - doc correction.

## pggap [open P3] protobuf file-set: paste-text path and stale-generation discard do not track the upload generation
Filed at rsu2 close (integrator, 2026-10-25). The multi-file upload set carries a generation counter; the paste-a-schema path and the discard/clear path do not advance or check the same generation, so a paste after a file-set upload (or a discard racing a re-upload) can leave the console compiling a stale mix. Fix: single generation for all schema-mutation paths, discard invalidates pending compiles.

## 0vzb.27 [open P3] Console corpus list omits the bundled BCheck set; desktop app does not attach it
Found while bundling the PortSwigger BCheck corpus (0vzb.21, commit 564cacd6). See its report and internal/bcheck/bundled/manifest.json reasons.

## 8yjj [open P4] api scan: a Fixed parameter is matched by name across the whole audit, not per endpoint
Existing backend behaviour, noted as not built in PR #342 (the dialog's hint says so).

## Evidence
A parameter marked Fixed for one endpoint in the review step is kept out of the insertion points of every endpoint with a parameter of that name.

## Consequence
Fixing a parameter on one endpoint silently stops it being attacked on the others.

## 86l0 [open P4] sitemap: an insert at a folder that already has observed traffic beneath it is stored and hidden, and answers already_seen:false
Follow-up from PR #343 (vc98).

## Evidence
Inserting an item at a folder path that already has observed traffic beneath it stores the item, which the read then hides, and the insert reply says already_seen:false.

## Consequence
The operator is told the insert added something new while nothing visible changed.

## dot6 [open P3] bcheck: collaborator-check limits after ar8v — not(x interactions) never fires, post-callback probes cannot be followed, Run test does not wait, given-response checks have no dispatcher
Known limits listed in PR #345 (ar8v).

## Evidence
1. not(x interactions) never fires: the claim ends outstanding (a miss, not a false positive).
2. A branch that needs a new probe after a callback cannot be followed and ends outstanding.
3. The console's Run test does not wait for interactions.
4. A given-response check with an interactions condition has nothing to dispatch it.

## Consequence
Some PortSwigger collaborator checks still never report, even when the callback arrives.

While T1 runs, I've scoped the next candidates. They're bigger:
- **`nulbyte`** (P2): null-byte XSS payload variants. It needs new fixtures modelled on VulnerableApp's img L5 and persistent L6 levels.
- **`o388-predial-vs-dial`** (P2): a residual list of sender connection-identity gaps. These are risk-path changes.

I'll stop after shipping this batch and check with you before taking those on.

**The batch so far** (on local branch `beads-batch2`, stacked on hotfix PR #367):
- **`8yjj`:** a parameter marked Fixed in the API scan review is now exempt only on the endpoint it was fixed on, not on every endpoint carrying that name.
- **`86l0`:** adding a site-map entry under a folder that already has traffic now answers "already seen" instead of storing an entry the map hides.
- **`credfx`:**
  - A retry that trips the crawl's pause policy now also stops the links that retry just found.
  - The "ignored second login form" record is pinned; it was already counted once per form, so only a test was needed.
  - A doc comment is corrected.
- **`pggap`:** a .proto file pick still loading can no longer overwrite a paste or a clear made after it.
- **`4xqt3-*`** (3 beads), GraphQL editor:
  - Two guard contracts are now pinned by tests: a check whose result is discarded still re-enables the buttons, and an Apply is discarded once the request changes, even if it changes back.
  - The unmount guard is added but untestable: React 18 drops those updates silently.
- **`0vzb.27`:** the 111 bundled BChecks that run in every audit now appear in the console's checks list, labelled "bundled". They can be switched off and viewed, but not edited or deleted.

Every fix has a test that fails without it. Lint reports 0 issues and `bun run check` passes. The bundle is rebuilt with bun 1.4.2.

**Hotfix PR #367:** CI is all green. It still needs an independent `agent-review` verdict; the session prompt I gave you earlier works if you swap in #367's head sha.

Once T1 passes, I'd push the batch. It can't go to master yet: it would either ride on #367, widening the review you need, or wait until #367 merges and go up as its own PR. I'll wait for #367 unless you'd rather combine them.

# Testing Strategy

Design effective testing strategies balancing coverage, speed, and maintenance.

## Testing Pyramid

```
        /  E2E  \         Few, slow, high confidence
       / Integration \     Some, medium speed
      /    Unit Tests  \   Many, fast, focused
```

## Strategy by Component Type

- **API endpoints**: Unit tests for business logic, integration tests for HTTP layer, contract tests for consumers
- **Data pipelines**: Input validation, transformation correctness, idempotency tests
- **Frontend**: Component tests, interaction tests, visual regression, accessibility
- **Infrastructure**: Smoke tests, chaos engineering, load tests

## What to Cover

Focus on: business-critical paths, error handling, edge cases, security boundaries, data integrity.

Skip: trivial getters/setters, framework code, one-off scripts.

## Output

Produce a test plan with: what to test, test type for each area, coverage targets, and example test cases. Identify gaps in existing coverage.

content.text:
I put three lenses on the repo: testing strategy, system design and architecture. The evidence is the package and test survey above, the CI workflows, and the defect classes the PR #363 review rounds actually found. I didn't run coverage tooling: the scanner suite alone takes about 15 minutes, and two agents are already using the machine.

## Testing strategy

**The current pyramid** has a wide unit layer and a narrow top:

| Layer | What exists | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| Unit and package | About 6,000 Go `Test*` functions (scanner 1,406, web 1,386, crawler 333, proxy 314, sender 260…), plus 180 UI test files | Every PR (the affected set) and every master push (full) |
| Integration / corpus | `vulnapp` fixtures with vulnerable/safe twins, and the runtime corpus tests (188 catalogue rows) | Every PR, in the `scanner-detect` shard |
| Race | `-race` on `internal/web` per PR; every other shard nightly | PR (web only) and nightly |
| UAT / E2E | `uat-cli`, 2 Playwright UAT specs, and `e2e-go.sh` nightly | PR (UAT) and nightly |
| Fuzz | 24 `Fuzz*` targets: proxy 5, httputil 5, http2 3, core 2, grpcproto 2… | Not part of the gate |

**Strengths worth keeping:**
- The vulnerable/safe-twin corpus. It's the right shape for a scanner: every detection claim has a false-positive control.
- Tests that fail loudly when a capability is missing (`TestDiscoveryCapabilityWasExercised`, and the corpus refusing to pass without Chrome), instead of skipping silently.
- The negative-control rule in T1 ("a test must fail without the fix").

**Gaps, ranked by the defects they let through:**

1. **27 Playwright specs in `ui/e2e/specs/` never run in CI.** `go.yml` runs only `npm run uat` (2 specs), so the broader browser suite is dead weight that will rot.
   - Plan: run `specs/` nightly in `nightly.yml`, or delete what's obsolete.
2. **Contract drift between the Go server and the TS client.** The Sequencer 400 came from the client's `manifestPatternFor` and the server's `routeRiskFor` disagreeing. The reviewer's 843-path cross-check found it, but no test pins it.
   - Plan: a contract test that dumps the server's resolution for every manifest key and its variants into a fixture, which the TS test asserts against. That runs on every PR, and either side drifting fails CI.
3. **Concurrency.** Today's defects included a data race (`sync.Map` reset), a deadlock (`PaceN`) and a fixpoint that never converged. `-race` covers only `web` per PR; `sender`, `intruder` and `proxy` see it only nightly.
   - Plan: move the `sender`, `intruder` and `proxy` race shards into the PR gate when those packages change. Adopt `testing/synctest` and goleak (bead `u5jf`) for timing-heavy tests.
4. **Vacuous tests.** I wrote three myself today: the CL.0 send-once test, the login-form record test and the unmount guard test. All passed without their fix.
   - Plan: make the negative control mechanical. A CI job on PRs that flips each touched `if` or condition (a cheap mutation pass with something like `go-mutesting` over changed lines) and reports surviving mutants as a warning first.
5. **Fuzzing isn't gated.** The parsers facing hostile input (HTTP framing, h2, gRPC, BCheck, OpenAPI) have targets, but nothing runs them. `scanner`, `bcheck`'s enumerator, `crawler`'s extraction and `web`'s JSON decoding have none.
   - Plan: a nightly fuzz job, 60 seconds per target with a corpus cache. Add targets for `bcheck.EnumerateWith`, `httputil.ReadResponseBody` and the OAuth/redirect parsers. This is bead `ibhs`.
6. **Scanner precision has no number.** The corpus tests pass or fail per row, but nothing tracks false-positive and false-negative rates over time. The `j1mk` parity epic exists, but the nightly VulnerableApp benchmark had a broken readiness probe until today.
   - Plan: publish the nightly scored run as an artifact with a trend, and fail on any regression against the pinned baseline (`compare_baseline.py` already exists).

**Coverage targets:** don't chase a percentage. Make these binding instead:
- 100% of catalogue rows with a vulnerable twin and a safe twin (already enforced).
- 100% of gated routes in the client/server contract fixture.
- Every risk-path package race-clean per PR.
- Every hostile-input parser with a fuzz target.

## System design

The flows run proxy → traffic store → scanner/intruder/crawler → web API → React console, plus the MCP and agent surfaces. The parts that are risky by design:

- **Many egress paths share one enforcement point.** Scope checks go through `probeGate`/`AuthoriseRaw` and the sender, but the review found bypasses where a new transport arrived: h3 ignored the upstream proxy and resolution override, and the sender's h3 pin did too. Every new protocol leg is a new chance to skip egress policy.
  - Design fix: a single `Dialer` interface that owns policy (scope, upstream, carrier, resolution, address family). No package may construct a transport without it, and a lint rule or test can enforce "no `http3.Transport` or `net.Dial` outside `sender/dial*`".
- **Network-settings changes vs. live connections** is the recurring `o388`/`h2sess-stamp` family: pools, H2 sessions and the ConnPool each stamp identity separately. One versioned "network generation" that every pooled connection is checked against would collapse three ad-hoc mechanisms into one.
- **Destructive-route gating lives in three places:** the Go manifest, the generated TS table and a hand-written TS resolver. The table is generated but the resolver isn't. Either generate the resolver too, or have the server resolve the route (`/api/routes/resolve?path=`) so the client never decides.

## Architecture

- **`internal/web` is a 50k-line flat package of 125 files that imports 42 internal packages.** It's the composition root, the HTTP layer and much of the feature logic at once (`api_toolkit.go` alone is 2,718 lines). That's why one review round touches a dozen unrelated files, and why `-race` on it is so expensive.
  - Recommendation: split by feature into subpackages (`web/apiscan`, `web/repeater`, `web/sitemap`…) behind one `Server` that only wires them. Do it incrementally; the `vnlh`/`fxxm` route-pattern work is the natural seam.
- **God files:** `crawler.go` (4,021 lines), `proxy.go` (3,850), `persist.go` (3,157) and `bcheck/insertion.go` (3,047). The h3 leg, the hook-drop hold and the truncation salvage all landed in `proxy.go`, and all three had review findings. Extracting `proxy/h3leg.go` and `proxy/intercept_hold.go` behind small interfaces would make each testable in isolation.
- **Dependency direction is healthy where it matters:** `core` imports nothing internal, and `sender` only 6. Keep it that way with an import-boundary test, a `go list` assertion that `sender` and `core` never import `web`, `scanner` or `proxy`.
- **Decision records:** `docs/adr` exists. The calls made this week aren't recorded anywhere outside PR threads: CL.0 gated under extended active, the IDOR "firm only with ownership" rule, and #363 merged over a `changes-required` verdict. They'd each be a short ADR.

## The six I'd do first

1. Run the 27 orphaned Playwright specs nightly, or delete them.
2. Add the client/server gated-route contract test.
3. Gate `-race` per PR for `sender`, `intruder` and `proxy` when they change.
4. Add a nightly fuzz job (`ibhs`).
5. Enforce the single egress `Dialer` with a test.
6. Start splitting `internal/web` along the routing seam.

The first three are small. I can turn any of these into beads or start on them. The two bead agents (`nulbyte`, `o388-predial`) and the batch T1 run are still going.
