  # Testing strategy review: burpsy (master 64af87c)
  
  I only read the repo. Nothing was edited, checked out or committed. The only things I ran were `go list` / `go test -list`, an AST scan for tests with no assertion path (in my scratchpad), and `go test -short -cover` on 29 small packages (writes to the Go cache only). That cover run had no Chrome, and `internal/dominvader` failed (see F1).
  
  ## Corrections to what was already known
  
  | Known claim | Verdict | What is actually true |
  |---|---|---|
  | 27 Playwright specs in `ui/e2e/specs` run in no CI job | **Confirmed, with one addition** | `uat-ui` (`go.yml:409-451`) runs only `specs-uat/` (2 files, 4 tests) via `playwright.uat.config.ts` (`testDir: "./specs-uat"`). `specs/` holds 27 files and about 92 tests and runs nowhere. Addition: `e2e/tsconfig.json:16` includes `["harness","specs","playwright.config.ts"]`, so `specs-uat/` and the UAT config are never type-checked. No CI job runs `npm run typecheck` for e2e at all. |
  | `-race` per PR only for `internal/web` | **Wrong** | Per PR (when affected) and on every master push, `race-web-0/1` and `race-core` run. `race-core` covers `internal/proxy`, `internal/dash` and `internal/pool` (`ci-shard.sh:57-59`). Everything else gets `-race` only nightly. Bead `racepr` asks for "sender, intruder and proxy", but proxy is already covered. See F2. |
  | 24 fuzz targets, no CI job runs them | **Wrong on both counts** | There are 21 `func Fuzz` targets. Nightly `fuzz` (`nightly.yml`, `scripts/ci-fuzz.sh`) fuzzes 10 of them for 5 minutes each. The other 11 run only their seed corpus as unit tests. See F3. |
  | No contract test between the UI gated-route resolver and the server's | **Confirmed, needs nuance** | The route *table* is contract-checked: `check:gated-routes` regenerates `gated-routes.ts` / `route-risk.ts` from `route_manifest.go` and `bun run check` fails on drift. The *resolver* (`api.ts:46-108`) is a hand port of `confirm_gate.go:331-500`, and each side is tested only on its own hand-written cases. Concrete divergences in F7. |
  | Three recent tests passed without their fix; the negative control is manual | **Confirmed** | `DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md:56` makes it a T1 manual step. No script or CI job automates it (bead `mutneg`). See F20. |
  
  ## (1) Inventory per package / area
  
  Tiers:
  - **T3-PR**: the affected set on a PR into master.
  - **T3-M**: the full suite on a push to master.
  - **N**: nightly.
  - **–**: nothing runs it.
  
  Coverage % is in-package statement coverage from my `-short -cover` run.
  
  | Package / area | Test types present | ~Tests (func Test) | CI tier | Notable gaps |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | internal/scanner | unit; integration against `internal/vulnapp` fixtures (declared vulns plus safe twins, coverage pinned at `wantDemonstrated = 188`); Chrome DOM; timing SQLi | 1406 (180 files) | 4 scanner shards T3-PR/M; `-race` N only | Race-only tests (`scanner_test.go:131`) are effective only nightly; 13 wall-clock assertions |
  | internal/web | httptest API; manifest invariants; confirm gate; source/byte guards | 1386 (293 files) | race-web-0/1 T3-PR/M | One test hits the public interactsh pool (F4); Chrome tests skip silently (F1); no egress-route scope matrix (F14); 82 `time.Sleep` |
  | internal/proxy | unit, in-process TLS MITM (`RootCAs` in 9 files), WS, H2, fuzz (5) | 314 (71 files) | race-core T3-PR/M | Absence-after-sleep asserts (F12); 54 sleeps, most of them poll loops |
  | internal/crawler | unit plus scope | 333 | rest; `-race` N | Characterization test that can only pass or skip (F13) |
  | internal/intruder | unit, scope | 304 | rest; `-race` N | Tight timing bounds (F21) |
  | internal/sender (the "one authorising path to a socket") | unit, scope refusal, redirect, H2, race-dependent tests | 260 | rest; `-race` N only | Tests claim they run under per-run race (F2) |
  | internal/core (traffic store, segment log) | unit, corruption/truncation, fuzz (2) | 240, 83.6% | rest; `-race` N | Capture files created world-readable, no permission test (F11) |
  | internal/session | unit, fuzz (1) | 182 | rest; `-race` N | One unconditional `t.Skip` stub (F13) |
  | internal/bcheck (+bundled) | unit, fuzz (1, unlisted) | 182 | rest | Fuzz never run (F3) |
  | internal/persist (project DB) | round-trip, migration, legacy rows, backup | 103, **63.0%** | rest | About 40 Save/Load pairs at 0% in-package (F10) |
  | internal/http2 / httputil | unit, fuzz (3 + 5) | 111 / 47, 90.5% / 83.7% | rest, nightly fuzz | 3 httputil fuzz targets unlisted, one with a committed crasher (F3) |
  | internal/sequencer, query, grpcproto, intercept, extension, mcp, agent, netauth, upstream, advisory, report, toollog, organizer, schedule, matchreplace, filelog, skills, servercerts, oob | unit (+ fuzz for query and grpcproto, unlisted) | 3–100 each; 68–96% | rest | `oob` live tests need build tag `oob_live`, which runs nowhere |
  | internal/tlsprobe | unit; live test against badssl.com behind `tlsx_live` | 10, 50.7% | rest; live –, by design | No hermetic substitute for the live path |
  | internal/wsclient | unit (clone only) | 3, **35.2%** | rest | `SendFrame`, `SendFrameWithHandshake`, `HandshakeRequest`, `authorityOf` at 0% |
  | internal/domexec, browser, blindxss, dominvader | real Chrome | 51 / 5 / 9 / 7 | rest | Three different no-Chrome policies (F1) |
  | internal/extscan | real ffuf/nuclei against loopback, skip ledger that fails the package | 33 | rest (tools installed) | This is the model the Chrome tests should copy |
  | internal/vulnapp | fixture target (48 source files) | 1 | rest | Exercised indirectly by the scanner, which is acceptable |
  | cmd/burpsy | CLI wiring, CLI scope refusal | 21 | rest | `main()` startup/restore (lines 42–~988) has no test and no restart test (F10) |
  | cmd/conform | unit | 10 | rest | – |
  | cmd/{burpsy-mcp, desktop, demo-target, openapi-dump, bcheck-bundle, live-test, xsschallenge, crawl-scan-demo, blindxss-demo}, internal/web/clickbandit | **none** | 0 | build/vet only | demo-target is the target the nightly parity bench depends on |
  | UI src/lib | bun unit (139 files) | ~1100 cases | `ui` job, every code change | – |
  | UI src/ui + src/pages | bun + happy-dom component tests (41 files) | ~330 cases | `ui` | 20 of 34 pages have no component test (F18) |
  | UI type/guards | tsc, tokens, gated-routes, api-types, biome, bundle freshness | – | `ui` (required) | e2e is not type-checked (above) |
  | Playwright `e2e/specs` | browser e2e, axe | 27 files / ~92 | **–** | Bead `e2eorph` |
  | Playwright `e2e/specs-uat` | browser UAT smoke | 2 files / 4 | `uat-ui` per change, **not required** | Flaked twice with cause not established (beads `uat-console-update-depth`, `uat-repeater-answer-expectation`) |
  | `scripts/uat-cli.sh` | binary UAT (exit codes, proxy, gated audit, XSS plus safe twin) | ~10 checks | `uat-cli` per change, **not required** | Never restarts the binary |
  | `e2e-go.sh` | binary + API e2e | 334 lines | N | No HTTPS, no restart |
  | `e2e.sh`, `e2e-audit.sh`, `e2e-scan.sh`, `e2e-tls.sh`, `e2e-intercept.sh` | e2e of the **frozen Rust binary** (`./target/debug/burpsy`) | – | `verify.sh` only, manual | Verify nothing about the Go product (F15) |
  | Fuzz | 21 targets | – | 10 in N | F3 |
  | bench-vulnapp / bench-parity | scored benchmark / parity report | – | N | No baseline exists, so the gate can never fail (F5) |
  | CI scripts | `beads-lint_test.py` | – | `beads` job | `ci-shard_test.sh`, `ci-fuzz_test.sh`, `capped-run_test.sh`, `ci-vulncheck-gate_test.py`, `bench/*_test.py` run nowhere. `affected-go-tests.sh`, `ci-changes.py`, `review-gate.sh` have no tests (F9) |
  
  Totals: 5,928 Go `func Test`, 72 `t.Skip` sites, 209 `time.Sleep` in tests (most of them poll loops). No `.only`, `.skip` or `.todo` in UI tests or specs. Only one Go test starts with an unconditional `t.Skip`.
  
  ## (2) Findings
  
  ### F1 chrome-skip-green — Browser-engine tests pass green when Chrome cannot launch — **major**
  **Evidence:**
  - `internal/domexec/browser_test.go:61-62`: `t.Skipf("no browser available, skipping: %v", sharedBrowserErr)`. All 35 `newTestBrowser(t)` callers in the DOM engine skip when *the package's own* `NewBrowser` fails.
  - `scripts/ci-install-tools.sh:50,73`: a failed Chrome warm-up only warns ("the tests decide"). It fails only when no binary exists on PATH.
  - The same bare-skip pattern appears in:
    - `remote_tab_close_test.go:47,66,114`
    - `blindxss/listener_test.go:72,143`
    - `scanner/frameable_browser_test.go:117`
    - `web/crawl_live_test.go:185`, `crawl_interact_route_test.go:94,135`, `api_recorded_login_test.go:277`
  - Policies are inconsistent:
    - `extscan/live_test.go:30-44` and `web/api_discovery_test.go:37-53` keep a skip ledger that fails the package.
    - `scanner/runtime_coverage_test.go:1097-1111` fails unless `BURPSY_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_COVERAGE=1`.
    - `dominvader` fails outright: my local run without Chrome gave `FAIL ... domexec: no chrome binary found` at `pollution_test.go:78,126`.
  
  **Risk:** a regression in `domexec.NewBrowser`, such as a launch flag that breaks headless start, makes it fail to launch. All 35 domexec tests then skip, and the `rest` shard goes green. The bug that matters becomes the reason the tests do not run.
  
  **Fix:**
  - Unit/harness: give `internal/domexec`, `internal/web`, `internal/blindxss` and `internal/browser` a `TestMain` skip ledger like extscan's. It fails the package when any capability skip happened, unless `BURPSY_ALLOW_NO_CHROME=1`.
  - Make the warm-up failure fatal in `ci-install-tools.sh`.
  - Example test: `TestBrowserCapabilityWasExercised`. It runs last through `TestMain` and does `if len(skips)>0 && os.Getenv("BURPSY_ALLOW_NO_CHROME")!="1" { fail("NOT exercised: "+strings.Join(skips,", ")) }`.
  - Negative control: in CI, run with `PATH` stripped of Chrome and expect red.
  
  ### F2 sender-race-claim — Race-dependent tests outside web/proxy/dash/pool run under `-race` only nightly, and some claim otherwise — **major**
  **Evidence:**
  - `internal/sender/close_delimited_race_test.go:10`: "Meaningful under -race (internal/sender runs in CI's race shard)".
  - `internal/sender/dial_identity_pin_test.go:181`: "only meaningful under -race, which the package gate runs".
  - `ci-shard.sh:162` (`rest_pkgs`) puts sender in `rest`, which runs without `-race` per PR and on master. `-race` happens only in `nightly.yml` `race (rest)`.
  - Other race-only regressions in the same position:
    - `scanner/scanner_test.go:131` (`TestRuntimeConfigEditIsAtomicAgainstTheDispatchCount`, which has no assertion other than the race detector)
    - `sitemap/concurrent_test.go:19`
    - `scanner/secrets_gitleaks_test.go:131`
  
  **Risk:** a PR reintroduces the unsynchronised read in sender's close-delimited path. The PR and the master push are green, nightly is red, and nothing files the failure (F17). The bad commit is already on master.
  
  **Fix:**
  - CI: add `internal/sender`, `internal/sitemap` and `internal/core` to `race-core` (all are small; measure first). For scanner, run `-race -run 'Atomic|Concurrent|Race'` on the race-only tests per PR.
  - Guard test in `ci-shard_test.sh`: every `_test.go` whose comment says "under -race" belongs to a package that a per-PR race shard owns.
  
  ### F3 fuzz-unlisted — 11 of 21 fuzz targets are never fuzzed, including one that already found a crash — **major**
  **Evidence:**
  - `scripts/ci-fuzz.sh:15-24` lists 10 targets.
  - Unlisted:
    - apidoc `FuzzParse`, bcheck `FuzzParse`
    - core `FuzzParse`, `FuzzParseWsFrameHeader`
    - grpcproto `FuzzDecode`, `FuzzParseProto`
    - httputil `FuzzSplitHeadBody`, `FuzzHeaderValue`, `FuzzHeaderValueExact`
    - query `FuzzParse`, session `FuzzJSONPath`
  - `internal/httputil/testdata/fuzz/FuzzHeaderValue/e2f5030826fd712c` is a committed crasher for a target the nightly job never fuzzes.
  - `ci-fuzz.sh verify` checks only that each listed target exists, not that each existing target is listed.
  - The fuzz job never saves the Go cache, so the fuzz corpus in `$GOCACHE/fuzz` starts from seeds every night.
  
  **Risk:** a regression in the WebSocket frame header parser (core) or the protobuf decoder (grpcproto), both of which parse attacker-supplied bytes, is never fuzzed.
  
  **Fix:**
  - In `verify`, add the reverse check: `grep -rhoE '^func Fuzz[A-Za-z0-9_]+' internal pkg`, and fail on any target missing from the list.
  - Fuzz all 21 targets as a matrix or at about 2 minutes each, so the job fits its 75-minute timeout.
  - Cache `~/.cache/go-build/fuzz` under a nightly key.
  
  ### F4 interactsh-public — A per-PR test registers with the real public interactsh pool and passes as a skip when the pool is down — **major** (guardrail)
  **Evidence:**
  - `internal/web/api_collaborator_batch_test.go:26-46`: `TestTheCollaboratorBatchMintAgainstThePublicPool` uses "the client's own default pool".
  - `ci-install-tools.sh:152-157` installs `interactsh-client`, so in CI the test is live.
  - Line 119-120: `if rec.Code == http.StatusServiceUnavailable { t.Skipf(...) }`.
  - It runs in `race-web-*` on every affected PR and every master push.
  
  **Risk:**
  - Every CI run makes a third-party registration. That breaks the "isolated lab only" rule, and it is a source of failures outside our control.
  - When the pool is down, the batch-mint contract goes unverified while CI reports green.
  
  **Fix:**
  - Integration test: start a local interactsh server in a container, or a recorded fake that serves `-json` output captured from the pinned v1.3.1 binary, at a loopback `ServerURL`.
  - Move the public-pool test behind `//go:build oob_live`.
  - Example test: `TestBatchMintSharesOneRegistrationAgainstALocalPool`. Mint `{"count":3}`, assert 3 addresses on one domain, 3 markers, and exactly 1 registration recorded by the fake.
  
  ### F5 bench-baseline-missing — The nightly scanner-quality regression gate cannot fail — **major**
  **Evidence:**
  - `nightly.yml` bench-vulnapp exits 0 on `rc=3` ("no baseline").
  - `scripts/bench/baseline/` contains only `vulnapp-image.txt`.
  - `git log --all -- scripts/bench/baseline/vulnapp.json` is empty: the baseline was never committed.
  
  **Risk:** true-positive or false-positive regressions against VulnerableApp go unnoticed indefinitely while the job is green.
  
  **Fix:** commit the first uploaded `vulnapp-*.json` as the baseline in a reviewed commit, and make `rc=3` a failure after a set date. The bench's own tests (`compare_baseline_test.py`, `run_vulnapp_test.py`, `parity_*_test.py`) should run in the `beads`-style Python job.
  
  ### F6 uat-not-required — The only binary-level and browser checks per PR do not block a merge — **major**
  **Evidence:**
  - `go.yml` `gate` has `needs: [changes, lint, test]`; neither `uat-cli` nor `uat-ui` is in it.
  - The header lists the required checks as `gate`, `ui`, `beads`, `review-gate`.
  - The `uat-cli` comment says to add `uat-cli` and `uat-ui` to the required checks to make them block a merge.
  - The 27 `specs/` files run nowhere, and e2e is not type-checked (table above). `ui-live.sh:4-8` records that two specs "named the consoleErrors fixture and never read it, so they asserted nothing".
  
  **Risk:** a console regression in Scope, Intercept retarget or Intruder hand-off merges green. Those specs (`scope.spec.ts`, `intercept-retarget.spec.ts`, `intruder-handoff.spec.ts`) exist but run nowhere, and `uat-ui` itself is advisory.
  
  **Fix:**
  - Add `uat-cli` and `uat-ui` to `gate.needs` or to branch protection.
  - Add `npm run typecheck` (with `specs-uat` in the include list) to `uat-ui`.
  - Run `specs/` nightly in a sharded job (about 10 minutes) with 0 retries.
  
  ### F7 gate-contract — The client resolver is a hand port of the server resolver, with no shared test vectors — **major**
  **Evidence:**
  - Go: `routeRiskFor` skips `"/"` outright (`confirm_gate.go:334`). TS: `manifestPatternFor` lets `"/"` match everything (`api.ts:49`).
  - Go resolves `r.URL.Path`, which is decoded (`confirm_gate.go:171`). TS resolves `new URL(url).pathname`, which is percent-encoded and has dot-segments resolved (`api.ts:100`). For `/api/x/a%2Fb` against a `{id}` pattern the two sides count different numbers of segments.
  - Ties: Go breaks them by `riskSeverity` (8 levels). TS breaks them by a gated boolean.
  - `gated-routes.test.ts:46-71` uses synthetic tables. The Go side has its own cases plus `TestRouteRiskForAgreesWithTheProductionMux`.
  
  **Risk:**
  - The server is authoritative, so there is no bypass.
  - But a client resolving a gated path to an ungated pattern sends no confirmation, and the operator gets a 428 instead of the confirmation dialog: the gated action is unusable from the console.
  - In the other direction, the console mints for the wrong pattern and the server refuses the spend.
  
  **Fix:** contract test. A Go test (`TestWriteResolverVectors` with `-update`) writes `internal/web/testdata/route-resolver-vectors.json` with `{path, pattern, gated}` for:
  - every manifest pattern instantiated (`{id}` → `7`, `{rest...}` → `""`, `"a/b"`, `{$}`)
  - plus the edge paths: `%2F`, `..`, trailing slash, `/confirm`, query strings.
  
  A bun test asserts `manifestPatternFor` and `gatedPatternFor` match every vector. Note that `testdata/` already forces a full CI run.
  
  ### F8 review-gate-risk-list — The gating predicate, token binding, and the tests that pin them are not risk paths — **major**
  **Evidence:** I evaluated `risk_of` from `scripts/review-gate.sh:52-114` on these paths, and every one returns no risk class:
  - `internal/web/agent_tools.go`, which holds `needsConfirmation` at line 128 (the set of gated risk classes)
  - `internal/web/confirm_binding.go` (token-to-call binding)
  - `confirm_gate_test.go`, `route_manifest_test.go`
  - `ui/src/lib/route-manifest.ts` (`gatedTable` and `parseGatedRiskClasses`, which build the client gate table)
  - `ui/src/lib/gated-routes.test.ts`
  - `scripts/ci/govulncheck-baseline.txt`, `scripts/ci-lint.sh`, `scripts/ci-fuzz.sh`
  
  Only `confirm_gate.go` itself matches.
  
  **Risk:** one PR can drop `riskDestructive` from `needsConfirmation` and update `agent_tools_test.go:67` and `gated-routes.test.ts:27` to match. Every destructive route is then ungated, CI is green, and no independent review is required. Likewise, a reachable vulnerability can be whitelisted by editing the baseline.
  
  **Fix:**
  - Add these paths, and a glob for `*_test.go` next to every listed source.
  - Add `scripts/review-gate_test.sh` (throwaway git repos, like `beads-lint_test.py`). Example: committing a change to `agent_tools.go` makes the script exit 1 with "risk-class paths touched".
  
  ### F9 ci-scripts-untested — The scripts that decide what CI runs have no tests, or tests that never run — **minor**
  **Evidence:**
  - No tests exist for `affected-go-tests.sh` (147 lines, which decides the PR test set), `ci-changes.py` (which decides whether Go jobs run at all) or `review-gate.sh`.
  - `ci-shard_test.sh`, `ci-fuzz_test.sh`, `capped-run_test.sh` and `ci-vulncheck-gate_test.py` exist, but no workflow invokes them.
  - `ci-shard.sh verify` (the shard-completeness proof) is mentioned only in a comment (`go.yml:160`); no job runs it.
  
  **Risk:** a selector bug, for example a new cross-directory read that no rule covers, silently narrows the PR test set. It surfaces only on the master push, after the merge.
  
  **Fix:**
  - A `ci-selftest` job running all `scripts/*_test.*` and `ci-shard.sh verify`.
  - Fixture-repo tests for `affected-go-tests.sh`. Example: changing `internal/core/x.go` lists `internal/core` and every reverse importer; changing `cmd/burpsy/main.go` lists `internal/proxy` through the explicit rule.
  
  ### F10 startup-restore-untested — Restoring persisted state at process start is untested — **major** (data integrity)
  **Evidence:**
  - The restore sequence runs inline in `main()` (`cmd/burpsy/main.go`, lines 42–~988):
    - `persistStore.Restore` (:294), `LoadFileLogging` (:309), `LoadUpstreamProxy` (:336)
    - `LoadCustomScanChecks` (:453), `LoadNetworkSettings` (:632), `LoadTlsPassthrough` / `LoadTlsPassthroughMode` (:892, :906), `LoadProxyOptions` (:918)
  - None of the 21 tests in `cmd/burpsy` starts the process twice. `e2e-go.sh` and `uat-cli.sh` start once and never reopen the same `-db`.
  - `internal/persist` is at 63.0%. At 0% in-package are `SavePlatformAuth`, `SaveClientCerts`, `SaveTlsPassthroughMode`, `SaveAuthzIdentities`, `SaveOrganizerCollections`, `SaveScanConfig`, `LoadInterceptLive`, and about 30 more Save/Load pairs. Of these, `SavePlatformAuth`, `SaveTlsPassthroughMode`, `SaveAuthzIdentities` and `SaveOrganizerCollections` are named by no test anywhere in the tree.
  
  **Risk:** an operator sets TLS pass-through mode, platform-auth credentials or authz identities and restarts. The setting comes back as its default, silently. For TLS pass-through, that means intercepting hosts the operator excluded.
  
  **Fix:**
  - Unit: extract the restore into `restoreState(p *persist.Store, deps) []restoreErr` and table-test every setting: save, reopen, restore, compare.
  - UAT: add a restart step to `uat-cli.sh` (start, set scope + proxy options + TLS pass-through, stop, start on the same `-db`, then GET each setting and compare).
  
  ### F11 capture-file-perms — Project and capture files have no permission test, and the code creates them world-readable — **major** (client data)
  **Evidence:**
  - `internal/core/segment.go:51` (`MkdirAll(dir, 0755)`), `:121` and `:150` (`OpenFile(..., 0644)`), `:286` (`os.Create`, 0666 &^ umask).
  - The SQLite project is opened with `sql.Open("sqlite", path)` (`persist.go:86`) with no mode.
  - The only permission assertions in tests are for `ca.key` (`proxy/cert_test.go:158`, `web/api_ca_test.go:112`, `api_ca_regenerate_test.go:85`).
  
  **Risk:** on a shared jump host, any local user can read captured client traffic, including session cookies and bearer tokens.
  
  **Fix:** product change plus a unit test. Example: `TestCaptureAndProjectFilesAreOwnerOnly` opens a project, captures one exchange, and asserts `mode&0o077 == 0` for the DB, the WAL/SHM files, every segment and the capture directory.
  
  ### F12 absence-after-sleep — "Nothing was recorded" assertions can pass while the bug is present — **minor**
  **Evidence:**
  - `proxy/webiface_test.go:81,180,206`: sleep 50ms, then assert the exchange count.
  - `proxy/options_scope_test.go:136-145` (`settleThenCountExchanges`, a 250ms settle used for the out-of-scope "not recorded" checks). Its own comment says these "can false-*pass*".
  - `proxy/page_observer_slot_test.go:100-104`.
  
  **Risk:** an out-of-scope request that *is* recorded, but more than 250ms late on a loaded runner, passes the scope test.
  
  **Fix:** a barrier. After the negative request, send an in-scope sentinel on the same listener, `waitForExchanges` for it, then assert the negative one is absent. Better, expose a record-decision hook (`recorded` / `dropped: out-of-scope`) and assert the decision event itself.
  
  ### F13 stub-and-vacuous — One stub test, and characterization tests that cannot fail — **minor**
  **Evidence:**
  - `session/tracer_test.go:90-92`: `TestTheRingIsBoundedAndNewestWins` is a bare `t.Skip`. The next test already covers the bound.
  - `crawler/js_extract_baseline_test.go:62-101` skips when the gap closes, so it can only pass or skip.
  - `scanner/scanner_test.go:131` asserts only through `-race`, which is nightly (F2).
  - `TestPageObserverSlotEmpty` (`page_observer_slot_test.go:110`) has no assertion path; found by an AST scan in which 11 of 5,928 tests had none, most of them legitimate helpers or `TestMain`.
  
  **Fix:**
  - Delete the stub.
  - Make the characterization test `t.Fatalf` when the gap closes, so the change is noticed.
  - Give the race-only test an explicit invariant: the count read equals the count of the snapshot it came from.
  
  ### F14 egress-matrix — No manifest-driven test that every egress or attack route refuses an out-of-scope target — **major**
  **Evidence:**
  - `route_manifest.go` has 28 `riskEgress` and 37 `riskAttack` routes.
  - Scope refusal is tested engine by engine, and well: `sender/authorised_test.go:70,193`, `intruder/engine_test.go:103`, `scanner/audit_engine_test.go:632,731`, `crawler/crawler_test.go:288`, `extscan/extscan_test.go:33`, `cmd/burpsy/cli` tests, `web/intruder_scope_test.go`, `web/session_scope_test.go`.
  - But `riskEgress` / `riskAttack` appear in tests only as classification checks (`agent_tools_test.go`, `route_manifest_test.go`). This overlaps bead `egressdial`.
  
  **Risk:** a new egress route builds its own transport (for example `repeater/ws-attach` or `apiscan/fetch`), skips `sender.Authorised`, and sends to an out-of-scope host. Its per-feature tests pass because they used an in-scope target.
  
  **Fix:** integration matrix test `TestEveryEgressAndAttackRouteRefusesAnOutOfScopeTarget`:
  - Iterate the manifest for routes in those two classes.
  - Each route has a minimal body template (required: a missing template fails the test).
  - Point the target at a loopback listener that is *excluded* from scope.
  - Mint a confirmation where the route is gated.
  - Assert a non-2xx refusal, or a reported refusal, and **zero accepted connections** on the listener.
  
  ### F15 legacy-e2e-rust — The root e2e suites test the frozen Rust binary — **minor**
  **Evidence:** `e2e.sh:41`, `e2e-audit.sh:94`, `e2e-scan.sh:39` and `e2e-tls.sh:53,107` launch `./target/debug/burpsy`; `e2e-intercept.sh:18` uses the cargo example. Only `e2e-go.sh` drives Go, and it has no HTTPS. `verify.sh:143` runs `go test ./...` without `-timeout 30m`.
  
  **Risk:** the full binary path (CA generated on first start, trusted by curl, then HTTPS through the proxy shows plaintext in history) has no Go equivalent in any tier. In-process coverage does exist in `internal/proxy` (`RootCAs` in 9 test files).
  
  **Fix:** port `e2e-tls.sh` into `e2e-go.sh`: curl with `--cacert $(GET /cert)` to a loopback TLS origin, then assert the plaintext path and body in `/api/history`. Add `-timeout 30m` to `verify.sh`.
  
  ### F16 doc-drift — The tier tables omit what CI actually runs — **minor**
  **Evidence:**
  - The T3 row in `DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md` §4 omits `uat-cli` and `uat-ui`.
  - The Nightly row lists only `e2e-go.sh` plus race, omitting `fuzz`, `bench-vulnapp` and `bench-parity`.
  - The CLAUDE.md tier table has the same omissions.
  
  **Fix:** update both tables. The F9 self-test could assert that the job names in `go.yml` and `nightly.yml` appear in §4.
  
  ### F17 nightly-no-alert — A red nightly reaches nobody — **minor**
  **Evidence:** `nightly.yml` has `permissions: contents: read` and no failure step. The header says "A red run here is a defect on master to file", but nothing files it.
  
  **Fix:** an `if: failure()` job with `issues: write`, or a bead-filing step, naming the job and the commit.
  
  ### F18 ui-page-tests — Several large pages have no rendered test in any CI tier — **minor**
  **Evidence:** no component test for `session.tsx` (2670 lines), `intercept.tsx` (1587), `organizer.tsx` (1415), `sitemap.tsx` (1397), `scope.tsx` (1211), `proxysettings.tsx` (701), `extensions.tsx` (698), `decoder.tsx`, `matchreplace.tsx` and 11 more. Their logic is partly tested in lib (`scope-*.test.ts`, `intercept-target.test.ts`, `sitemap-*.test.ts`). Their Playwright specs run nowhere (F6).
  
  **Fix:** component test per page for render, empty, failed and loading states. Example: `scope.test.tsx` mocks `/api/scope` with a 500 and asserts the page shows a failure banner, not "No rules".
  
  ### F19 live-only-paths — Some paths are verified only by tests that never run — **minor**
  **Evidence:**
  - `//go:build oob_live` (`internal/oob/live_test.go`)
  - `//go:build tlsx_live` (`tlsprobe_live_test.go`, against badssl.com)
  - `H2TEST_LIVE` (`http2/h2test/zz_live_origin_test.go:15`)
  - `tlsprobe` is at 50.7% and `wsclient` at 35.2%, with `SendFrame` at 0%.
  
  Not running third-party-live tests in CI is correct under the guardrails.
  
  **Fix:** hermetic substitutes:
  - tlsx against a loopback `httptest.NewUnstartedServer` with expired, self-signed and wrong-host certs
  - a wsclient `SendFrame` round trip against a local WS echo server
  
  ### F20 negative-control-manual (known, bead `mutneg`) — **major**
  **Evidence:** `DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md:56` (T1, "revert the fix, watch it fail"). No automation in `scripts/` or the workflows.
  
  **Fix:** a CI "red on base" job. For test functions a PR adds or changes:
  1. Check out the merge-base's non-test `.go` files, keeping the PR's `_test.go` files.
  2. Run `go test -run '^(NewTests)$'`.
  3. Require failure or a compile error. A pass is reported as "test does not exercise the change", and an explicit `negative-control: n/a <reason>` line in the PR body overrides it.
  
  ### F21 timing-bounds — Tight wall-clock upper bounds, which nightly `-race` runs amplify — **minor**
  **Evidence:**
  - `intruder/retry_test.go:104` (`elapsed >= 120ms` for a whole `Run`)
  - `intruder/limit_group_test.go:97,170` (500ms)
  - `scanner/auto_backoff_test.go:81` (500ms)
  - scanner shards run at `-parallel 12`, with the "flake-watch" note at `ci-shard.sh:79`
  
  `uat-ui` already flaked twice in CI with the cause not established.
  
  **Fix:** use an injectable clock in intruder retry and backoff, and assert on the clock's recorded sleeps instead of wall time.
  
  ## (3) Recommended coverage targets
  
  | Area | Target |
  |---|---|
  | Security boundaries (sender authorisation, `confirm_gate.go`, `confirm_binding.go`, scope matching, `agent_tools.go needsConfirmation`) | 100% branch on refusal paths; the F14 manifest matrix covers 100% of egress and attack routes; F7 vectors cover 100% of manifest patterns; mutation score ≥ 90% on these files (F20) |

  | internal/core (store, segments) | Keep ≥ 85%; add a file-mode test (F11) |
  | internal/proxy, sender, http2, httputil | ≥ 85%; every parser of untrusted bytes has a fuzz target that runs nightly (21 of 21) |
  | internal/scanner | Keep the pinned demonstrated-row floor (188) plus a safe twin per row; a committed bench baseline whose regressions fail nightly |
  | Small packages (wsclient, tlsprobe, alpn, advisory, apidoc) | ≥ 70% with hermetic tests |
  | cmd/* | `burpsy-mcp`, `desktop` and `demo-target` get a build-and-start smoke test (start, hit one endpoint, exit 0) |
  | UI | Every page has a component test for render, empty, failed and loading; lib ≥ 80%; e2e type-checked in CI; `specs/` nightly; `uat-*` required |
  | Race | Every package with goroutines or mutexes and a race-dependent test is in a per-PR race shard |
  | Skips | Zero silent capability skips in CI: every package with a capability skip has a ledger that fails the run |
  
  Relevant files: `/home/user/burpsy/.github/workflows/go.yml`, `/home/user/burpsy/.github/workflows/nightly.yml`, `/home/user/burpsy/scripts/ci-shard.sh`, `/home/user/burpsy/scripts/ci-fuzz.sh`, `/home/user/burpsy/scripts/review-gate.sh`, `/home/user/burpsy/scripts/ci-install-tools.sh`, `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/internal/web/confirm_gate.go`, `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/src/lib/api.ts`, `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/internal/web/ui/e2e/tsconfig.json`, `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/internal/domexec/browser_test.go`, `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/internal/web/api_collaborator_batch_test.go`, `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/internal/core/segment.go`, `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/cmd/burpsy/main.go`, `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/internal/sender/close_delimited_race_test.go`.

# Testing strategy review: burpsy (master 64af87c)

I only read the repo. Nothing was edited, checked out or committed. The only things I ran were `go list` / `go test -list`, an AST scan for tests with no assertion path (in my scratchpad), and `go test -short -cover` on 29 small packages (writes to the Go cache only). That cover run had no Chrome, and `internal/dominvader` failed (see F1).

## Corrections to what was already known

| Known claim | Verdict | What is actually true |
|---|---|---|
| 27 Playwright specs in `ui/e2e/specs` run in no CI job | **Confirmed, with one addition** | `uat-ui` (`go.yml:409-451`) runs only `specs-uat/` (2 files, 4 tests) via `playwright.uat.config.ts` (`testDir: "./specs-uat"`). `specs/` holds 27 files and about 92 tests and runs nowhere. Addition: `e2e/tsconfig.json:16` includes `["harness","specs","playwright.config.ts"]`, so `specs-uat/` and the UAT config are never type-checked. No CI job runs `npm run typecheck` for e2e at all. |
| `-race` per PR only for `internal/web` | **Wrong** | Per PR (when affected) and on every master push, `race-web-0/1` and `race-core` run. `race-core` covers `internal/proxy`, `internal/dash` and `internal/pool` (`ci-shard.sh:57-59`). Everything else gets `-race` only nightly. Bead `racepr` asks for "sender, intruder and proxy", but proxy is already covered. See F2. |
| 24 fuzz targets, no CI job runs them | **Wrong on both counts** | There are 21 `func Fuzz` targets. Nightly `fuzz` (`nightly.yml`, `scripts/ci-fuzz.sh`) fuzzes 10 of them for 5 minutes each. The other 11 run only their seed corpus as unit tests. See F3. |
| No contract test between the UI gated-route resolver and the server's | **Confirmed, needs nuance** | The route *table* is contract-checked: `check:gated-routes` regenerates `gated-routes.ts` / `route-risk.ts` from `route_manifest.go` and `bun run check` fails on drift. The *resolver* (`api.ts:46-108`) is a hand port of `confirm_gate.go:331-500`, and each side is tested only on its own hand-written cases. Concrete divergences in F7. |
| Three recent tests passed without their fix; the negative control is manual | **Confirmed** | `DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md:56` makes it a T1 manual step. No script or CI job automates it (bead `mutneg`). See F20. |

## (1) Inventory per package / area

Tiers:
- **T3-PR**: the affected set on a PR into master.
- **T3-M**: the full suite on a push to master.
- **N**: nightly.
- **–**: nothing runs it.

| `e2e.sh`, `e2e-audit.sh`, `e2e-scan.sh`, `e2e-tls.sh`, `e2e-intercept.sh` | e2e of the **frozen Rust binary** (`./target/debug/burpsy`) | – | `verify.sh` only, manual | Verify nothing about the Go product (F15) |

Totals: 5,928 Go `func Test`, 72 `t.Skip` sites, 209 `time.Sleep` in tests (most of them poll loops). No `.only`, `.skip` or `.todo` in UI tests or specs. Only one Go test starts with an unconditional `t.Skip`.

## (2) Findings

### F1 chrome-skip-green — Browser-engine tests pass green when Chrome cannot launch — **major**
**Evidence:**
- `internal/domexec/browser_test.go:61-62`: `t.Skipf("no browser available, skipping: %v", sharedBrowserErr)`. All 35 `newTestBrowser(t)` callers in the DOM engine skip when *the package's own* `NewBrowser` fails.
- `scripts/ci-install-tools.sh:50,73`: a failed Chrome warm-up only warns ("the tests decide"). It fails only when no binary exists on PATH.
- The same bare-skip pattern appears in:
  - `remote_tab_close_test.go:47,66,114`
  - `blindxss/listener_test.go:72,143`
  - `scanner/frameable_browser_test.go:117`
  - `web/crawl_live_test.go:185`, `crawl_interact_route_test.go:94,135`, `api_recorded_login_test.go:277`
- Policies are inconsistent:
  - `extscan/live_test.go:30-44` and `web/api_discovery_test.go:37-53` keep a skip ledger that fails the package.
  - `scanner/runtime_coverage_test.go:1097-1111` fails unless `BURPSY_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_COVERAGE=1`.
  - `dominvader` fails outright: my local run without Chrome gave `FAIL ... domexec: no chrome binary found` at `pollution_test.go:78,126`.

**Risk:** a regression in `domexec.NewBrowser`, such as a launch flag that breaks headless start, makes it fail to launch. All 35 domexec tests then skip, and the `rest` shard goes green. The bug that matters becomes the reason the tests do not run.

**Fix:**
- Unit/harness: give `internal/domexec`, `internal/web`, `internal/blindxss` and `internal/browser` a `TestMain` skip ledger like extscan's. It fails the package when any capability skip happened, unless `BURPSY_ALLOW_NO_CHROME=1`.
- Make the warm-up failure fatal in `ci-install-tools.sh`.
- Example test: `TestBrowserCapabilityWasExercised`. It runs last through `TestMain` and does `if len(skips)>0 && os.Getenv("BURPSY_ALLOW_NO_CHROME")!="1" { fail("NOT exercised: "+strings.Join(skips,", ")) }`.
- Negative control: in CI, run with `PATH` stripped of Chrome and expect red.

### F2 sender-race-claim — Race-dependent tests outside web/proxy/dash/pool run under `-race` only nightly, and some claim otherwise — **major**
**Evidence:**
- `internal/sender/close_delimited_race_test.go:10`: "Meaningful under -race (internal/sender runs in CI's race shard)".
- `internal/sender/dial_identity_pin_test.go:181`: "only meaningful under -race, which the package gate runs".
- `ci-shard.sh:162` (`rest_pkgs`) puts sender in `rest`, which runs without `-race` per PR and on master. `-race` happens only in `nightly.yml` `race (rest)`.
- Other race-only regressions in the same position:
  - `scanner/scanner_test.go:131` (`TestRuntimeConfigEditIsAtomicAgainstTheDispatchCount`, which has no assertion other than the race detector)
  - `sitemap/concurrent_test.go:19`
  - `scanner/secrets_gitleaks_test.go:131`

**Risk:** a PR reintroduces the unsynchronised read in sender's close-delimited path. The PR and the master push are green, nightly is red, and nothing files the failure (F17). The bad commit is already on master.

**Fix:**
- CI: add `internal/sender`, `internal/sitemap` and `internal/core` to `race-core` (all are small; measure first). For scanner, run `-race -run 'Atomic|Concurrent|Race'` on the race-only tests per PR.
- Guard test in `ci-shard_test.sh`: every `_test.go` whose comment says "under -race" belongs to a package that a per-PR race shard owns.

### F3 fuzz-unlisted — 11 of 21 fuzz targets are never fuzzed, including one that already found a crash — **major**
**Evidence:**
- `scripts/ci-fuzz.sh:15-24` lists 10 targets.
- Unlisted:
  - apidoc `FuzzParse`, bcheck `FuzzParse`
  - core `FuzzParse`, `FuzzParseWsFrameHeader`
  - grpcproto `FuzzDecode`, `FuzzParseProto`
  - httputil `FuzzSplitHeadBody`, `FuzzHeaderValue`, `FuzzHeaderValueExact`
  - query `FuzzParse`, session `FuzzJSONPath`
- `internal/httputil/testdata/fuzz/FuzzHeaderValue/e2f5030826fd712c` is a committed crasher for a target the nightly job never fuzzes.
- `ci-fuzz.sh verify` checks only that each listed target exists, not that each existing target is listed.
- The fuzz job never saves the Go cache, so the fuzz corpus in `$GOCACHE/fuzz` starts from seeds every night.

**Risk:** a regression in the WebSocket frame header parser (core) or the protobuf decoder (grpcproto), both of which parse attacker-supplied bytes, is never fuzzed.

**Fix:**
- In `verify`, add the reverse check: `grep -rhoE '^func Fuzz[A-Za-z0-9_]+' internal pkg`, and fail on any target missing from the list.
- Fuzz all 21 targets as a matrix or at about 2 minutes each, so the job fits its 75-minute timeout.
- Cache `~/.cache/go-build/fuzz` under a nightly key.

### F4 interactsh-public — A per-PR test registers with the real public interactsh pool and passes as a skip when the pool is down — **major** (guardrail)
**Evidence:**
- `internal/web/api_collaborator_batch_test.go:26-46`: `TestTheCollaboratorBatchMintAgainstThePublicPool` uses "the client's own default pool".
- `ci-install-tools.sh:152-157` installs `interactsh-client`, so in CI the test is live.
- Line 119-120: `if rec.Code == http.StatusServiceUnavailable { t.Skipf(...) }`.
- It runs in `race-web-*` on every affected PR and every master push.

**Risk:**
- Every CI run makes a third-party registration. That breaks the "isolated lab only" rule, and it is a source of failures outside our control.
- When the pool is down, the batch-mint contract goes unverified while CI reports green.

**Fix:**
- Integration test: start a local interactsh server in a container, or a recorded fake that serves `-json` output captured from the pinned v1.3.1 binary, at a loopback `ServerURL`.
- Move the public-pool test behind `//go:build oob_live`.
- Example test: `TestBatchMintSharesOneRegistrationAgainstALocalPool`. Mint `{"count":3}`, assert 3 addresses on one domain, 3 markers, and exactly 1 registration recorded by the fake.

### F5 bench-baseline-missing — The nightly scanner-quality regression gate cannot fail — **major**
**Evidence:**
- `nightly.yml` bench-vulnapp exits 0 on `rc=3` ("no baseline").
- `scripts/bench/baseline/` contains only `vulnapp-image.txt`.
- `git log --all -- scripts/bench/baseline/vulnapp.json` is empty: the baseline was never committed.

**Risk:** true-positive or false-positive regressions against VulnerableApp go unnoticed indefinitely while the job is green.

**Fix:** commit the first uploaded `vulnapp-*.json` as the baseline in a reviewed commit, and make `rc=3` a failure after a set date. The bench's own tests (`compare_baseline_test.py`, `run_vulnapp_test.py`, `parity_*_test.py`) should run in the `beads`-style Python job.

### F6 uat-not-required — The only binary-level and browser checks per PR do not block a merge — **major**
**Evidence:**
- `go.yml` `gate` has `needs: [changes, lint, test]`; neither `uat-cli` nor `uat-ui` is in it.
- The header lists the required checks as `gate`, `ui`, `beads`, `review-gate`.
- The `uat-cli` comment says to add `uat-cli` and `uat-ui` to the required checks to make them block a merge.
- The 27 `specs/` files run nowhere, and e2e is not type-checked (table above). `ui-live.sh:4-8` records that two specs "named the consoleErrors fixture and never read it, so they asserted nothing".

**Risk:** a console regression in Scope, Intercept retarget or Intruder hand-off merges green. Those specs (`scope.spec.ts`, `intercept-retarget.spec.ts`, `intruder-handoff.spec.ts`) exist but run nowhere, and `uat-ui` itself is advisory.

**Fix:**
- Add `uat-cli` and `uat-ui` to `gate.needs` or to branch protection.
- Add `npm run typecheck` (with `specs-uat` in the include list) to `uat-ui`.
- Run `specs/` nightly in a sharded job (about 10 minutes) with 0 retries.

### F7 gate-contract — The client resolver is a hand port of the server resolver, with no shared test vectors — **major**
**Evidence:**
- Go: `routeRiskFor` skips `"/"` outright (`confirm_gate.go:334`). TS: `manifestPatternFor` lets `"/"` match everything (`api.ts:49`).
- Go resolves `r.URL.Path`, which is decoded (`confirm_gate.go:171`). TS resolves `new URL(url).pathname`, which is percent-encoded and has dot-segments resolved (`api.ts:100`). For `/api/x/a%2Fb` against a `{id}` pattern the two sides count different numbers of segments.
- Ties: Go breaks them by `riskSeverity` (8 levels). TS breaks them by a gated boolean.
- `gated-routes.test.ts:46-71` uses synthetic tables. The Go side has its own cases plus `TestRouteRiskForAgreesWithTheProductionMux`.

**Risk:**
- The server is authoritative, so there is no bypass.
- But a client resolving a gated path to an ungated pattern sends no confirmation, and the operator gets a 428 instead of the confirmation dialog: the gated action is unusable from the console.
- In the other direction, the console mints for the wrong pattern and the server refuses the spend.

**Fix:** contract test. A Go test (`TestWriteResolverVectors` with `-update`) writes `internal/web/testdata/route-resolver-vectors.json` with `{path, pattern, gated}` for:
- every manifest pattern instantiated (`{id}` → `7`, `{rest...}` → `""`, `"a/b"`, `{$}`)
- plus the edge paths: `%2F`, `..`, trailing slash, `/confirm`, query strings.

A bun test asserts `manifestPatternFor` and `gatedPatternFor` match every vector. Note that `testdata/` already forces a full CI run.

**Evidence:** I evaluated `risk_of` from `scripts/review-gate.sh:52-114` on these paths, and every one returns no risk class:
- `internal/web/agent_tools.go`, which holds `needsConfirmation` at line 128 (the set of gated risk classes)
- `internal/web/confirm_binding.go` (token-to-call binding)
- `confirm_gate_test.go`, `route_manifest_test.go`
- `ui/src/lib/route-manifest.ts` (`gatedTable` and `parseGatedRiskClasses`, which build the client gate table)
- `ui/src/lib/gated-routes.test.ts`
- `scripts/ci/govulncheck-baseline.txt`, `scripts/ci-lint.sh`, `scripts/ci-fuzz.sh`

Only `confirm_gate.go` itself matches.

**Risk:** one PR can drop `riskDestructive` from `needsConfirmation` and update `agent_tools_test.go:67` and `gated-routes.test.ts:27` to match. Every destructive route is then ungated, CI is green, and no independent review is required. Likewise, a reachable vulnerability can be whitelisted by editing the baseline.

**Fix:**
- Add these paths, and a glob for `*_test.go` next to every listed source.
- Add `scripts/review-gate_test.sh` (throwaway git repos, like `beads-lint_test.py`). Example: committing a change to `agent_tools.go` makes the script exit 1 with "risk-class paths touched".

### F9 ci-scripts-untested — The scripts that decide what CI runs have no tests, or tests that never run — **minor**
**Evidence:**
- No tests exist for `affected-go-tests.sh` (147 lines, which decides the PR test set), `ci-changes.py` (which decides whether Go jobs run at all) or `review-gate.sh`.
- `ci-shard_test.sh`, `ci-fuzz_test.sh`, `capped-run_test.sh` and `ci-vulncheck-gate_test.py` exist, but no workflow invokes them.
- `ci-shard.sh verify` (the shard-completeness proof) is mentioned only in a comment (`go.yml:160`); no job runs it.

**Risk:** a selector bug, for example a new cross-directory read that no rule covers, silently narrows the PR test set. It surfaces only on the master push, after the merge.

**Fix:**
- A `ci-selftest` job running all `scripts/*_test.*` and `ci-shard.sh verify`.
- Fixture-repo tests for `affected-go-tests.sh`. Example: changing `internal/core/x.go` lists `internal/core` and every reverse importer; changing `cmd/burpsy/main.go` lists `internal/proxy` through the explicit rule.

### F10 startup-restore-untested — Restoring persisted state at process start is untested — **major** (data integrity)
**Evidence:**
- The restore sequence runs inline in `main()` (`cmd/burpsy/main.go`, lines 42–~988):
  - `persistStore.Restore` (:294), `LoadFileLogging` (:309), `LoadUpstreamProxy` (:336)
  - `LoadCustomScanChecks` (:453), `LoadNetworkSettings` (:632), `LoadTlsPassthrough` / `LoadTlsPassthroughMode` (:892, :906), `LoadProxyOptions` (:918)
- None of the 21 tests in `cmd/burpsy` starts the process twice. `e2e-go.sh` and `uat-cli.sh` start once and never reopen the same `-db`.
- `internal/persist` is at 63.0%. At 0% in-package are `SavePlatformAuth`, `SaveClientCerts`, `SaveTlsPassthroughMode`, `SaveAuthzIdentities`, `SaveOrganizerCollections`, `SaveScanConfig`, `LoadInterceptLive`, and about 30 more Save/Load pairs. Of these, `SavePlatformAuth`, `SaveTlsPassthroughMode`, `SaveAuthzIdentities` and `SaveOrganizerCollections` are named by no test anywhere in the tree.

**Risk:** an operator sets TLS pass-through mode, platform-auth credentials or authz identities and restarts. The setting comes back as its default, silently. For TLS pass-through, that means intercepting hosts the operator excluded.

**Fix:**
- Unit: extract the restore into `restoreState(p *persist.Store, deps) []restoreErr` and table-test every setting: save, reopen, restore, compare.
- UAT: add a restart step to `uat-cli.sh` (start, set scope + proxy options + TLS pass-through, stop, start on the same `-db`, then GET each setting and compare).

### F11 capture-file-perms — Project and capture files have no permission test, and the code creates them world-readable — **major** (client data)
**Evidence:**
- `internal/core/segment.go:51` (`MkdirAll(dir, 0755)`), `:121` and `:150` (`OpenFile(..., 0644)`), `:286` (`os.Create`, 0666 &^ umask).
- The SQLite project is opened with `sql.Open("sqlite", path)` (`persist.go:86`) with no mode.
- The only permission assertions in tests are for `ca.key` (`proxy/cert_test.go:158`, `web/api_ca_test.go:112`, `api_ca_regenerate_test.go:85`).

**Risk:** on a shared jump host, any local user can read captured client traffic, including session cookies and bearer tokens.

**Fix:** product change plus a unit test. Example: `TestCaptureAndProjectFilesAreOwnerOnly` opens a project, captures one exchange, and asserts `mode&0o077 == 0` for the DB, the WAL/SHM files, every segment and the capture directory.

### F12 absence-after-sleep — "Nothing was recorded" assertions can pass while the bug is present — **minor**
**Evidence:**
- `proxy/webiface_test.go:81,180,206`: sleep 50ms, then assert the exchange count.
- `proxy/options_scope_test.go:136-145` (`settleThenCountExchanges`, a 250ms settle used for the out-of-scope "not recorded" checks). Its own comment says these "can false-*pass*".
- `proxy/page_observer_slot_test.go:100-104`.

**Risk:** an out-of-scope request that *is* recorded, but more than 250ms late on a loaded runner, passes the scope test.

**Fix:** a barrier. After the negative request, send an in-scope sentinel on the same listener, `waitForExchanges` for it, then assert the negative one is absent. Better, expose a record-decision hook (`recorded` / `dropped: out-of-scope`) and assert the decision event itself.

- `crawler/js_extract_baseline_test.go:62-101` skips when the gap closes, so it can only pass or skip.
- `scanner/scanner_test.go:131` asserts only through `-race`, which is nightly (F2).

**Fix:**
- Delete the stub.
- Make the characterization test `t.Fatalf` when the gap closes, so the change is noticed.
- Give the race-only test an explicit invariant: the count read equals the count of the snapshot it came from.

### F14 egress-matrix — No manifest-driven test that every egress or attack route refuses an out-of-scope target — **major**
**Evidence:**
- `route_manifest.go` has 28 `riskEgress` and 37 `riskAttack` routes.
- Scope refusal is tested engine by engine, and well: `sender/authorised_test.go:70,193`, `intruder/engine_test.go:103`, `scanner/audit_engine_test.go:632,731`, `crawler/crawler_test.go:288`, `extscan/extscan_test.go:33`, `cmd/burpsy/cli` tests, `web/intruder_scope_test.go`, `web/session_scope_test.go`.

- Each route has a minimal body template (required: a missing template fails the test).

- Mint a confirmation where the route is gated.

**Evidence:** `e2e.sh:41`, `e2e-audit.sh:94`, `e2e-scan.sh:39` and `e2e-tls.sh:53,107` launch `./target/debug/burpsy`; `e2e-intercept.sh:18` uses the cargo example. Only `e2e-go.sh` drives Go, and it has no HTTPS. `verify.sh:143` runs `go test ./...` without `-timeout 30m`.

2. Run `go test -run '^(NewTests)$'`.

`bead/nulbyte` is merged into `beads-batch2` (merge commit). The build and `go vet` pass, and gofmt is clean under go1.27.3. The one gofmt hit came from an older gofmt binary on the path, not the project's toolchain.

The agent's own run of `internal/scanner` and `internal/vulnapp` passed. That run includes the full fixture corpus, with the coverage floor of 188 detected rows enforced. Each new test failed with the null-byte code switched off and passed again with it restored.

The new null-byte payloads now find both VulnerableApp levels burpsy used to miss, and none of the safe twins is flagged. The separate stored-XSS check still has no null-byte payloads, so I'll file that as a follow-up bead.

The testing-strategy review is back with 21 findings, F1 to F21. It also corrects two things we had assumed:

- **Race checks per PR:** `-race` already runs per PR on proxy, dash and pool (plus `internal/web`), not on web alone. What gets `-race` only nightly is sender, sitemap, core and scanner, yet two sender tests' comments claim they run under it per PR.
- **Fuzzing:** there are 21 fuzz targets, not 24. Nightly fuzzes 10 of them, and the other 11 never run, including one with a crash input already committed.

New risks it found that no bead covers yet:

- Browser-engine tests pass green when Chrome can't launch; 35 domexec tests just skip.
- A per-PR test registers with the real public interactsh pool.
- The nightly benchmark can never fail, because no baseline was ever committed.
- The `uat-cli` and `uat-ui` checks don't block merges.
- Gating code such as `agent_tools.go needsConfirmation` and `confirm_binding.go` isn't on the review-gate's list of risky paths.
- Settings restored at startup are untested; four Save/Load pairs have no test anywhere.
- Capture files are created world-readable.
- There's no test that every egress or attack route refuses an out-of-scope target.

The system-design review is still running. When it's in, I'll merge the three reviews into one report, publish it, file the new findings as P1 beads, and start the fixes in parallel.

  - **Fix:** OpenAPI and MCP derive from `needsConfirmation` only; delete the dead gate; decide on execute explicitly and update the comment.

  - I did not review the client-facing h2 leg, intruder `ConnPool` beyond the o388 notes (which I left alone as instructed), or BCheck corpus depth.

  - F4, F5, F6, F7, F10 and F12 are from reading the code and were not run.

  - **Evidence:**
    - `Put` holds `ts.mu` across `Parse`, `segmentLog.Append` and the SQLite `INSERT` (`store.go:899-956`, `persist.go:692-711`, single connection at `persist.go:90`). Resident mode inserts the blob, up to 64 MiB.

    - Reserve slots in the index without holding the global lock across I/O.
    - Move the durable mirror and passive scanning to bounded asynchronous queues, with backpressure and counters for dropped or pending work.
    - Make segment-backed capture the default.

  - **Evidence:**
    - `needsConfirmation` (`agent_tools.go:128-135`) covers scope, attack, credential and destructive only.
    - The `riskExecute` comment calls it "confirmation-worthy" (`route_manifest.go:47-56`), while a test pins it as excluded (`agent_tools_test.go:103-112`).
    - The OpenAPI generator (`openapi.go:194-196`) tells clients every class except read and asset needs a confirmation. That is false for local, egress and execute. The generated `ui/src/lib/api-schema.d.ts:927,947` says `/api/extensions/load` needs one.
    - A second gate implementation, `confirmationGate{confirmed map}` (`agent_tools.go:116-157`), has no production caller (only `agent_tools_test.go`). Tests assert a control that never runs.
  - **Failure scenario:** an MCP agent can start an allowlisted plugin process (`/api/extensions/load`, `/invoke`) with no confirmation, while the published contract says one is required. Reviewers reading the schema believe Repeater sends are gated.

  - **Evidence:** `api_tools.go:277-284` uses `MayContainHost`, while the group keep-alive mode runs `AuthoriseRaw` per request (`api_repeater_group.go:446`).
  - **Failure scenario:** a path exclude such as `/admin/delete` blocks the group mode but not a single send to the same bytes.
  - **Fix:** call `AuthoriseRaw` in the shared send-spec builder.

  - **Evidence:** segment directory 0755 and files 0644 / `os.Create` (`core/segment.go:51,121,150,286`); the SQLite project file uses default permissions (`persist.go:86`). The CA key, by contrast, is 0600.

  - **Fix:** 0700 directories and 0600 files.

  1. **No crash containment, and wire parsing duplicated across five-plus parsers (F1).** One hostile byte sequence ends the process. Fix it with one strict parser, `recover` at goroutine roots, and fuzzing.
  2. **Persistence coupled into the store lock and the relay goroutine (F2, F9).** This produces a proven deadlock now and global serialisation at scale. The mirror should be an asynchronous, owned writer rather than a callback run under a lock.
  3. **Egress policy enforced per call site rather than by construction (F4, F5, F6, plus the known h3 case).** The same "gate on policy, forget the carrier" bug already fixed in one sender path survives in two others. Browser and subprocess egress sit entirely outside the `egressdial` plan. The fix is one Dialer plus one scope-gating loopback proxy for everything not written in Go.
  4. **The console trusts any client that reads (F3), and confirmation is not tied to a human.** Any caller that passes the same-origin check can request a token and spend it immediately; for MCP the only human step is whatever the host shows for `burpsy_confirm`. This is the open bead 2jrr.2.
  5. **The gating policy has several sources of truth (F10):** the Go predicate, the manifest comments, OpenAPI, the TypeScript resolver, and a test-only gate.
  6. **Proxy resource bounds (F7, F8):** no timeouts, an unbounded connection count, and silent truncation on HTTP/1.
  
  ### What I did not do
  - I did not run the full suite or `-race`.
  - I did not review the client-facing h2 leg, intruder `ConnPool` beyond the o388 notes (which I left alone as instructed), or BCheck corpus depth.
  - The pool-desync variant of F8 was not reproduced.
  - F4, F5, F6, F7, F10 and F12 are from reading the code and were not run.

  ## System-design review of burpsy-go: flows, findings, ranked risks
  
  I found three blockers, and I reproduced all three at runtime:
  - **Hostile chunk size crashes the process.** A response with chunk size `-1` panics the shared HTTP/1 parser, and nothing recovers the panic on the proxy or scanner paths.
  - **Project switch deadlocks.** Switching projects while traffic is being captured hangs the whole process.
  - **DNS rebinding reads captured traffic.** A hostile page can read captured traffic, cookies and credentials from the console with GET requests, because the Host check only applies to POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
  
  On egress I found more bypasses than the known h3 one:
  - HTTPS traffic through the proxy skips a SOCKS-only setting.
  - The headless browser's renders are not scope-gated.
  - The browser session's scope-gate proxy, nuclei and ffuf all dial directly.
  
  I did not modify `/home/user/burpsy`. The repros ran in a tar copy of `burpsy-go` under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-burpsy/66b7b689-6882-5e3a-8187-823ee0e17adf/scratchpad/mod/burpsy-go`.     - `forwardRequest` (`:3618`) uses one fresh connection per request.

  | Browser scope-gate proxy | `domexec/session.go:419,486` | yes | none (direct dial) |
  | nuclei / ffuf | `extscan/nuclei.go:184`, `ffuf.go:149` | target check plus result filter afterwards | none (F6) |
  | testssl / sslyze | `tlsprobe/tlsprobe.go:186` | yes | none |

## System-design review of burpsy-go: flows, findings, ranked risks

I found three blockers, and I reproduced all three at runtime:
- **Hostile chunk size crashes the process.** A response with chunk size `-1` panics the shared HTTP/1 parser, and nothing recovers the panic on the proxy or scanner paths.
- **Project switch deadlocks.** Switching projects while traffic is being captured hangs the whole process.
- **DNS rebinding reads captured traffic.** A hostile page can read captured traffic, cookies and credentials from the console with GET requests, because the Host check only applies to POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.

On egress I found more bypasses than the known h3 one:
- HTTPS traffic through the proxy skips a SOCKS-only setting.
- The headless browser's renders are not scope-gated.
- The browser session's scope-gate proxy, nuclei and ffuf all dial directly.

I did not modify `/home/user/burpsy`. The repros ran in a tar copy of `burpsy-go` under `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-burpsy/66b7b689-6882-5e3a-8187-823ee0e17adf/scratchpad/mod/burpsy-go`. The scratch test files are `internal/web/zz_switch_deadlock_scratch_test.go`, `internal/web/zz_rebind_scratch_test.go`, `internal/sender/zz_negchunk_scratch_test.go` and `internal/sender/zz_capdesync_scratch_test.go`. A standalone chunk-parser repro is in `.../scratchpad/chunk/`. All paths below are relative to `/home/user/burpsy/burpsy-go/`.

### 1. Flows

**(a) Traffic capture**
- **Listener and connections.** The accept loop in `internal/proxy/listeners.go:421` starts one goroutine per connection (`go s.handleConnectionOn`). `handleConnectionOn` (`proxy.go:1474`) puts a 30s deadline on the request line only (`proxy.go:1488-1500`). From there it splits into CONNECT (`handleConnect`, then `interceptTLS` at `proxy.go:1579` or `tunnelConnection` at `:2203`) and plain HTTP (`handleHTTP` at `:2280`).
- **Upstream forwarding.**
  - `forwardRequest` (`:3618`) uses one fresh connection per request.
  - `forwardOnly` (`:3479`) handles out-of-scope traffic, which is forwarded but not recorded.
  - The h3 Alt-Svc leg is `forwardH3` (`:3715`), gated by `h3EgressPossible` (`:3589`).
- **TLS dials and certificates.** Upstream TLS dials go through `dialUpstreamTLS` (`tls_dial.go:124`, using `alpn.Dialer`). Interception leaf certificates come from `TlsEngine.GetCertificate` (`proxy.go:318`), and the CA is loaded once in `cmd/burpsy/main.go`.
- **WebSocket.** `ws.go` / `ws_live.go`, with frame reassembly capped in `core/websocket.go:305`.
- **Rewrites and hooks.** Match & replace (`proxy.go:2796`), the response rules, the traffic hook (`traffic_hook.go:113`, panic-contained) and the intercept hold (`intercept/intercept.go:846`, `Wait()` with no timeout; pending response holds capped at 256 by `:935`).
- **Recording.** `record()` (`proxy.go:2885`) calls `scanner.Capture.Record` (`scanner/capture.go:270`), which writes `TrafficStore.Put`/`AddExchange` and then runs the passive scan and static DOM analysis (`capture.go:486`). This happens synchronously on the relay goroutine, after the response has been written to the client (`proxy.go:2157-2164`, `2674-2677`).

**(b) Egress**

| Surface | Path | Scope | Upstream policy / SOCKS / resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| Typed and raw sender | `sender/sender.go` (`buildClient` at :284, raw dial at :630) | `AuthorisedSender` (`authorised.go`) | yes, except the gaps in F4 |
| Crawler | `crawler.go:3801` (`AuthorisedSender`, per-authority limiter) | yes | yes |
| Scanner probes | `scanner.go:878` `probeGate` (`AuthorisedSender` + `ContextPacer`) | yes | yes |
| Repeater | `web/api_tools.go:432` (raw `SendRawOutcome`) | host-level only (F10) | yes |
| Intruder | `AuthorisedSender` plus caller-owned `ConnPool` | yes | stamped (o388) |
| Proxy upstream | `proxy/tls_dial.go` | n/a | plaintext yes; TLS skips a SOCKS-only setting (F4) |
| h3 Alt-Svc leg | proxy and sender | n/a | known; now gated off when a policy or carrier is set |
| Browser renders | `domexec/taint.go:833` | top-level URL only (F5) | none |
| Browser scope-gate proxy | `domexec/session.go:419,486` | yes | none (direct dial) |
| nuclei / ffuf | `extscan/nuclei.go:184`, `ffuf.go:149` | target check plus result filter afterwards | none (F6) |
| testssl / sslyze | `tlsprobe/tlsprobe.go:186` | yes | none |
| Collaborator client | `oob/client.go:254` | n/a | none; defaults to the public OAST pool (`client.go:97-99`) |
| Collaborator health, password-reset mailbox, LLM triage | `api_collaborator_health.go:76`, `checks_pwreset.go:1657`, `triage.go:110` | operator infrastructure | direct, by design |

**F1 `negchunk-panic`: a negative chunk size panics and kills the process — BLOCKER**

input.prompt:

input.prompt:
Repo /home/user/burpsy (Go module burpsy-go, GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3). Create branch bead/config-release from local branch beads-batch2 (HEAD 0c33fab) in your worktree. Fix two P1 beads (.beads/issues.jsonl):
1. burpsy-react-ui-scanconfig-persist-format: internal/persist/persist.go:2609-2625 saves json.Marshal(scanner.ScanConfig) (68 fields, almost no json tags → Go field names on disk) and loads into a fresh &scanner.ScanConfig{}; internal/web/project_state.go:28-31 then replaces the launch baseline with it. Also test a renamed/unknown key doesn't break loading.
