It goes through the existing `dialPlain`, so the upstream proxy policy, SOCKS carrier and resolution table all apply. It is wired in `cmd/burpsy/main.go`, `cli.go` and `web/api_recorded_login.go`.
  - **The three callers:**
    - The crawl renderer gates on the crawl's scope. Refused requests become a per-page skip record in the crawler.
    - The rendered-DOM audit and the CSTI check use a new `scanner/render_gate.go`. It checks each subrequest with `AuthoriseRaw`, and allows only the page's own origin when no scope is declared.
    - The audit counts pages that had something refused (`rendered_audit.scope_blocked`).
  
  ## Bead 2: nuclei and ffuf bypassed the egress policy
  - **Per-run gate.** Every `RunNuclei`/`RunFFUF` starts an egressgate proxy with a scope gate (`internal/extscan/egress.go`). It is passed as `nuclei -proxy` and `ffuf -x`.
    - Refused requests are never dialled.
    - Allowed ones go through `Config.EgressDial`, wired to the sender in `cli_extscan.go` and `web/api_discovery.go`.
  - **nuclei runs HTTP templates only (`-pt http`).** Its dns/tcp/ssl/headless/code templates would connect around an HTTP proxy. This narrows what a nuclei run covers.
  - **New default rate of 50 requests/s** (`DefaultNucleiRateLimit`), instead of nuclei's own 150.
  - **HTTPS can only be checked per connection.** Inside an HTTPS tunnel the gate sees host and port, not the path. So an HTTPS target on a host that is only partly in scope is now refused before launch. Before, such a subtree was scanned.
  - **Reporting.** Results carry `EgressGate`, `GateRefused` and `GateRefusals`.
    - A nuclei run with any refusals is reported as partial (`IncompleteScopeRefused`), so the CLI exits non-zero. Expect this often: nuclei templates that request the host root are refused whenever the target is a subpath.
    - The CLI and the discovery summary print what was refused.
  - **Unchanged:** the after-the-fact hit filter stays as a second layer.
  
  ## Tests (T1)
  - `gofmt -l` with the go1.27.3 toolchain is clean, and `go vet ./...` passes.
  - `scripts/affected-go-tests.sh 163acf1` gave 22 packages; `go test -count=1 -timeout 40m` on them exited 0 with no SKIPs. Scanner took 1386s, web 209s, domexec 122s.
  - Chrome came from `/opt/pw-browsers` on PATH (it is not otherwise installed).
  - I set `BURPSY_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_EXTSCAN=1` because ffuf and nuclei aren't installed here. Without it, `TestExternalToolCapabilitiesWereExercised` fails for that reason alone.
  
  New tests:
  - `domexec/render_gated_test.go`: an in-scope page pulls a script, image, iframe, fetch and XHR from an out-of-scope loopback port. The test counts zero accepted connections there, checks the in-scope script still ran, and checks the refusal is named. A second test covers refusing an out-of-scope target and a nil gate.
  - `egressgate/egressgate_test.go`: in-scope plain and CONNECT requests are forwarded through the injected dialer. An out-of-scope host, an excluded path and an out-of-scope CONNECT get a 403 with zero connections and zero dials.
  - `sender/egress_dial_test.go`: the dial goes through the configured upstream proxy.
  - `scanner/render_gate_test.go` and `crawler/render_blocked_test.go`.
  - `extscan/egress_test.go`: the nuclei/ffuf argument builders include the proxy flag, `-pt http` and the default `-rl`; the gate refuses and forwards correctly through the dialer; HTTPS on a partly scoped host is refused before launch.
  - `extscan/egress_unix_test.go`: fake nuclei and ffuf scripts curl through the passed flag. Zero connections reach the out-of-scope host, the in-scope request arrives, and the refusal is counted and makes the run partial.
  
  ## Negative controls (each one failed as expected, then was restored)
  - Render routed back through the ungated path: the out-of-scope host accepted 4 connections.
  - Gate built without the egress dialer: 0 dials, fails.
  - `EgressDialContext` dialling directly: upstream proxy saw nothing, fails.
  - Render-gate `AllowURL` always allowing: three out-of-scope URLs allowed, fails.
  - Crawler skip record removed: fails.
  - egressgate `AllowURL` check bypassed: 200 instead of 403, fails.
  - nuclei without `-proxy` and ffuf without `-x`: both the argument tests and the end-to-end tests fail.
  - extscan gate allowing everything: the out-of-scope host accepted a connection.
  
  ## Leftovers (also written into `burpsy-go/gaps.md`; no beads filed, since I was told not to touch issues.jsonl)
  1. **Other navigations in the shared browser are still ungated**, with Chrome dialling directly: `ObserveTaint`, `ObserveStored` (the stored-XSS render pass), `SubmitAndObserve`, `NavigateSPA`, `ObserveCrossOriginReferers`, `RenderFragment` and `Browser.Interact`. This needs a follow-up bead.
  2. **Remote CDP engines** gate renders with Fetch interception only, so out-of-process frames and workers are not seen.
  3. **Excluded paths inside HTTPS tunnels** are not enforced for extscan. Closing this needs TLS interception in egressgate.
  4. **ffuf has no default rate cap.**
  5. **`tlsprobe` and `oob`** still dial on their own; `oob` defaults to the public OAST pool.
  6. **Not tested against real binaries:** the real nuclei/ffuf flags (`-proxy`, `-pt`, `-x`) are unverified, because I was not allowed to `go install` ffuf. Checking them against real binaries is still outstanding.
  
  Per-render isolated contexts may slow renders somewhat; I didn't measure a baseline (the CSTI browser test took 62s).
  
  The scratchpad is shared with another agent's session: someone overwrote my `gt.sh` there. My later helper files use an `egress_a53_` prefix.

content.content:
# Not required by branch protection: a scheduled run is attached to no pull request.
#
#   e2e-go   e2e-go.sh against a local target.
#   bench-vulnapp  the scored VulnerableApp benchmark against the tracked baseline (scripts/bench).
#   fuzz     every fuzz target for 2 minutes each, one process per target (scripts/ci-fuzz.sh).
#   race     every go.yml test shard except race-web-0/1 and race-core, under -race (CI_SHARD_RACE=1). With
#            race-web and race-core on every push to master, the race detector covers the whole module.
#
# There is no separate plain (non-race) full-suite job: the push to master already runs the full
# suite on the commit this run tests, and the race run executes the same tests again (a superset,
# as in go.yml's reasoning for dropping the plain internal/web shard).

on:
  schedule:
    # 03:17 UTC. Off the hour on purpose: scheduled runs at :00 are the ones GitHub delays or drops
    # under load.
    - cron: "17 3 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # e2e-go.sh builds the real binary and drives it end to end against a local Python target on
  # 127.0.0.1 (ports 18180/18181/18199): proxy capture, history, audit, repeater, intruder,
  # sequencer, the cookie jar, stats. It needs only go, python3 and curl, all on the runner. It
  # reaches no host but loopback.
  e2e-go:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20

input.command:
python3 - <<'E'
p='.github/workflows/nightly.yml'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""#   race     every go.yml test shard except race-web-0/1 and race-core, under -race (CI_SHARD_RACE=1). With
#            race-web and race-core on every push to master, the race detector covers the whole module.
""","""#   race     every go.yml test shard except race-web-0/1 and race-core, under -race (CI_SHARD_RACE=1). With
#            race-web and race-core on every push to master, the race detector covers the whole module.
#   report   when any job above fails, opens (or comments on) one `nightly-failure` issue naming the
#            failed jobs and the commit, so a red night reaches someone instead of sitting in the tab.
""",1)
s=s.rstrip("\n")+"""

  # A red nightly is a defect on master to file (header). This job files it: one open issue labelled
  # nightly-failure collects every red night (a new comment per run) until someone closes it. Only
  # this job gets issues:write; the workflow default stays contents:read.
  report:
    needs: [e2e-go, race, bench-vulnapp, bench-parity, fuzz]
    if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'schedule' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: File or update the nightly-failure issue
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RESULTS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          failed=$(jq -r 'to_entries[] | select(.value.result == "failure" or .value.result == "cancelled") | .key' <<<"$RESULTS" | paste -sd, -)
          body="Nightly failed on ${SHA} — jobs: ${failed:-unknown}. Run: ${RUN_URL}"
          gh label create nightly-failure --color B60205 --description "A scheduled nightly run failed" 2>/dev/null || true
          open=$(gh issue list --label nightly-failure --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number')
          if [ -n "$open" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$open" --body "$body"
          else
            gh issue create --title "Nightly failing on master" --label nightly-failure --body "$body"
          fi
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
E

lines: // Put stores a raw HTTP message and returns its ID.
+// put is Put without taking the capture gate: the caller holds it (CaptureHold).
+// addExchange is AddExchange without taking the capture gate: the caller holds it (CaptureHold).
+// CaptureHold keeps the capture gate held across several writes that belong together — one
+// exchange's request, response, earlier stages and index row — so a project switch can never fall
+// between them and leave the messages in one project and the exchange row in the other
+// (burpsy-react-ui-capture-split). Its Put and AddExchange do not take the gate again: a
+// sync.RWMutex read side is not reentrant once a writer is queued, so re-entering would deadlock
+// against a waiting switch. Release exactly once, and before anything that may take the gate on
+// another store (a passive scan adding findings).
+// HoldCapture takes the capture gate (a no-op without one) and returns the hold.
+// Put stores a message under the hold.
+// AddExchange adds an exchange row under the hold.
+// Release lets the gate go. Safe to call more than once.

lines: // reqTLS is the destination's scheme, and it is a variable rather than the literal `true` this
// said so. Reading the message once and parsing the Host out of the bytes keeps a

// with the option off a listener that was sent an origin-form request it
// be decoded again at each of those. The rewiring is a rewrite of `Content-Length` alone; the
// original chunk-size and chunk extensions are not preserved, because the head no longer advertises
+// maxRequestHeadBytes bounds a request's line plus header block, as httputil.MaxResponseHeadBytes
+var errRequestHeadTooLarge = errors.New("proxy: request head exceeds the size limit")
+// readHeadLine reads one line through its '\n', refusing to buffer more than limit bytes of it.
+// readFullRequest returns nil when the request head is larger than maxRequestHeadBytes; the caller
+	// Read headers, bounded in total (burpsy-react-ui-proxy-no-timeouts): a client streaming header
+	// lines without end used to grow this buffer until the process ran out of memory, and on a
+	// non-loopback listener that client need not be the operator. A head past the cap is refused
+	// (nil), the same bound MaxResponseHeadBytes puts on what an origin can send back.
// in this package could only ever be a way for the row and the message it
// indexes to disagree about the same bytes. Its three test cases moved with it,
+// writeHeadTooLarge answers a request whose head passed maxRequestHeadBytes. Best effort: the caller
+// closes the connection either way, and the unread remainder of the head makes it unusable.

Content-Length: 0
Connection: close

"))

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# uat-cli.sh — UAT for the burpsy CLI (bead burpsy-react-ui-uat1): build the real binary and use it
# the way an operator does, against a fixture target, checking findings and exit codes. Not a unit
# suite. Run from anywhere; needs go, python3 and curl. Reaches loopback only.
#
#   1. exit codes: `-scan-config list` exits 0 and prints configurations; an unknown flag and a
#      `-store-verify` of a missing directory exit non-zero; an empty one exits 0.
#   2. proxy: a request sent through the proxy reaches the fixture target (internal/vulnapp, the
#      deliberately vulnerable app) verbatim and is captured in history.
#   3. scan: an audit of that exchange (through the confirmation gate) reports the reflected
#      cross-site scripting the target declares at /search, and none on its safe twin.
#
# Ports (distinct from e2e-go.sh 18180s and the browser UAT harness 18280s): proxy 18380, web 18381,
# target 18399. e2e-go.sh stays the broad API suite (nightly); this is the short operator flow a
# pull request runs.
set -uo pipefail
repo=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PROXY_PORT=${UAT_PROXY_PORT:-18380}
WEB_PORT=${UAT_WEB_PORT:-18381}
TARGET_PORT=${UAT_TARGET_PORT:-18399}
PASS=0; FAIL=0
ok() { echo "  PASS  $1"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); }
no() { echo "  FAIL  $1"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }

work=$(mktemp -d)
cleanup() {
  [ -n "${TARGET_PID:-}" ] && kill "$TARGET_PID" 2>/dev/null
  [ -n "${BURPSY_PID:-}" ] && kill "$BURPSY_PID" 2>/dev/null
  wait 2>/dev/null
  if [ "$FAIL" -ne 0 ]; then echo "--- burpsy log"; tail -60 "$work/burpsy.log" 2>/dev/null; fi
  rm -rf "$work"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

echo "=== build ==="
if ! (cd "$repo/burpsy-go" && go build -o "$work/burpsy" ./cmd/burpsy && go build -o "$work/demo-target" ./cmd/demo-target) 2>"$work/build.log"; then
  head -20 "$work/build.log"; echo "  FAIL  go build"; exit 1
fi
ok "burpsy and demo-target build"

echo "=== 1. exit codes ==="
out=$("$work/burpsy" -scan-config list 2>&1); rc=$?
{ [ $rc -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$out" ]; } && ok "-scan-config list exits 0 and prints configurations" || no "-scan-config list: rc=$rc"
"$work/burpsy" -no-such-flag >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
[ $rc -ne 0 ] && ok "an unknown flag exits non-zero ($rc)" || no "an unknown flag exited 0"
mkdir "$work/empty-dir"
"$work/burpsy" -store-verify "$work/empty-dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
[ $rc -eq 0 ] && ok "-store-verify of a directory with no segments exits 0 (nothing to fault)" || no "-store-verify of an empty directory: rc=$rc"
"$work/burpsy" -store-verify "$work/no-such-dir" >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
[ $rc -ne 0 ] && ok "-store-verify of a directory that does not exist exits non-zero ($rc)" || no "-store-verify of a missing directory exited 0"

echo "=== 2. proxy a request to the fixture target ==="
"$work/demo-target" -addr "127.0.0.1:$TARGET_PORT" >"$work/target.log" 2>&1 & TARGET_PID=$!
"$work/burpsy" -db "$work/uat.db" -proxy "127.0.0.1:$PROXY_PORT" -web "127.0.0.1:$WEB_PORT" \
  -scope-include 127.0.0.1 >"$work/burpsy.log" 2>&1 & BURPSY_PID=$!
for _ in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$WEB_PORT/api/stats" && break; sleep 0.1; done
for _ in $(seq 1 100); do curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$TARGET_PORT/" && break; sleep 0.1; done
body=$(env -u NO_PROXY -u no_proxy curl -s -x "http://127.0.0.1:$PROXY_PORT" "http://127.0.0.1:$TARGET_PORT/search?q=seed")
echo "$body" | grep -q 'seed' && ok "the proxied response reached the client" || no "proxied body: ${body:0:120}"
sleep 0.5
read -r XID <<<"$(python3 - "$WEB_PORT" <<'PY'
import json,sys,urllib.request
rows=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{sys.argv[1]}/api/history",timeout=10))
rows=rows if isinstance(rows,list) else (rows.get("exchanges") or [])
row=next((r for r in rows if r.get("path","").startswith("/search")),None)
print(row["id"] if row else "none")
PY
)"
[ "$XID" != none ] && ok "the exchange is in history (id $XID)" || { no "no /search exchange in history"; echo "############ $PASS passed, $FAIL failed ############"; exit 1; }

echo "=== 3. scan the exchange ==="
# history_id PREFIX -> the id of the first history exchange whose path starts with PREFIX, or "none".
history_id() {
  python3 - "$WEB_PORT" "$1" <<'PY'
import json,sys,urllib.request
rows=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{sys.argv[1]}/api/history",timeout=10))
rows=rows if isinstance(rows,list) else (rows.get("exchanges") or [])
row=next((r for r in rows if r.get("path","").startswith(sys.argv[2])),None)
print(row["id"] if row else "none")
PY
}
# audit_exchange ID LABEL -> audits one exchange through the confirmation gate (refused unconfirmed
# first), returning non-zero when it could not run.
audit_exchange() {
  local id="$1" label="$2" code token res
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:$WEB_PORT/api/audit/$id")
  [ "$code" = 428 ] && ok "an unconfirmed audit of $label is refused (428)" || no "unconfirmed audit of $label -> HTTP $code, want 428"
  token=$(python3 - "$WEB_PORT" "$id" <<'PY'
import json,sys,urllib.request
web,xid=sys.argv[1:3]
d={"method":"POST","url":f"/api/audit/{xid}"}
r=urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{web}/api/audit/confirm",json.dumps(d).encode(),{"content-type":"application/json"}),timeout=10)
print(json.load(r).get("token",""))

)
  [ -n "$token" ] || { no "could not mint a confirmation for the audit of $label"; return 1; }
  res=$(curl -s -m 300 -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:$WEB_PORT/api/audit/$id" -H "X-Burpsy-Confirm: $token")
  echo "$res" | grep -q "\"exchange_id\":$id" && ok "the audit of $label ran" || { no "audit of $label response: ${res:0:160}"; return 1; }
  LAST_FOUND=$(python3 -c 'import json,sys;print(json.loads(sys.argv[1]).get("outcome",{}).get("findings",-1))' "$res")
  # Coverage: an audit that ran no active checks, or errored on some, proves nothing about a clean result.
  python3 -c '
import json,sys
d=json.loads(sys.argv[1]); b=(d.get("breakdown") or {}).get("breakdown") or {}
sys.exit(0 if d.get("active_checks",0)>0 and b.get("errored",1)==0 else 1)' "$res" && ok "the audit of $label ran active checks with none errored" || no "audit of $label ran no active checks or some errored: ${res:0:200}"
}
# xss_on ID -> reflected cross-site scripting issues that carry an occurrence on exchange ID. /api/issues
# lists every occurrence of an issue with its exchange_id, so this is per exchange: unlike the totals it is
# not collapsed by the de-duplication across exchanges.
xss_on() {
  curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:$WEB_PORT/api/issues" | python3 -c '
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
want=int(sys.argv[1])
print(sum(1 for f in d.get("findings",[]) if "cross-site scripting" in (f.get("check_name") or f.get("issue_name") or "").lower() and any(o.get("exchange_id")==want for o in f.get("occurrences",[]))))' "$1"
}
# xss_count [PATH] -> cross-site scripting findings, optionally only those naming PATH.
xss_count() {
  curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:$WEB_PORT/api/findings" | python3 -c '
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)

# ADR 0002 — The CL.0 smuggled-prefix probe runs only under CheckExtendedActive

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-27
- **Context artefacts:** PR #363 review (`checks_smuggling.go:346`), commits `393d2ed1`, `324fa6f0`

## Context

`CheckRequestSmuggling` promises that nothing is queued on a back-end connection: CL.TE, TE.CL and
the HTTP/2 downgrades are detected by timing against a consistently framed control. The CL.0
smuggled-prefix probe (`checks_smuggling_cl0.go`) is different. The scanner owns only the
client-side socket; behind a front end that pools back-end connections and honours
`Content-Length`, the smuggled canary's answer can wait on a SHARED back-end connection and arrive
in the response slot of another user's request.

Backlog work re-enabled the probe inside the plain smuggling run, with a finding text claiming
"nothing was queued for any other user's connection".

## Decision

1. The CL.0 probe is not part of `CheckRequestSmuggling`. It runs only under
   `CheckExtendedActive`, the opt-in that already admits "Client-side desync", and the
   `ScanConfig` doc for that switch names the shared-connection risk.
2. The two rows that read the probe share one result per endpoint (`cl0Probes`), so the prefix is
   sent once, however many rows report from it.
3. Finding and code comments say plainly that the probe can leave a response on a pooled back-end
   connection. They never claim it stays on the scanner's connection.

## Consequences

- A plain smuggling run no longer reports CL.0. Operators who want it opt into extended active.
- `TestCL0NeedsTheExtendedActiveOptIn` and `TestCL0ProbeIsSentOncePerEndpoint` pin both rules.

# ADR 0006 — burpsy-go is the product; crates/ is a frozen parity oracle

- **Status:** Accepted (recorded retroactively, 2026-10-27; Bead: adr-backfill)
- **Context artefacts:** `AGENTS.md` (the two-tree table), `burpsy-go/gaps.md`, `scripts/review-gate.sh` (crates/ refused), ADR 0001

## Context

burpsy was first written in Rust (`crates/`, 13 crates, ~68k lines). The Go port in `burpsy-go/` overtook it:
the console, the scanner corpus and every feature since 2026-10-12 exist only in Go. Two trees that both
look buildable invite work in the wrong one, and the release workflow still built the Rust CLI until
`release-ships-rust` (ce12d6b).

## Decision

1. `burpsy-go/` is the only implementation that ships and the only one that receives features.
2. `crates/` is frozen: it is read as the specification when Go behaviour is ambiguous, and measured
   against through `burpsy-go/gaps.md` (ADR 0001). The review gate refuses any change under `crates/`.
3. Releases build the Go binaries (`cmd/burpsy`, `cmd/burpsy-mcp`), stamped with the tag (`internal/buildinfo`).

## Consequences

- The Rust crate boundaries ("the crate split enforces the dependency direction") no longer enforce
  anything; the Go layering is enforced by `internal/archtest` and the core/sender import tests instead.
- `verify.sh` and the root `e2e*.sh` suites still drive the Rust binary (bead `legacy-e2e-rust`).
E
cat > 0007-memory-authoritative-store-sqlite-mirror.md <<'E'
# ADR 0007 — Memory is authoritative; SQLite is a durable mirror

- **Status:** Accepted (recorded retroactively, 2026-10-27; Bead: adr-backfill)
- **Context artefacts:** `burpsy-go/docs/DATA-MODEL.md` §"Memory is authoritative", `internal/core/store.go`, `internal/persist`, `internal/web/api_project_open.go`

## Context

Capture is the hot path: every proxied exchange is stored before the next keep-alive request is read.
A database round trip on that path, or a database as the read model for history, would put SQLite in
front of every console read and every capture.

## Decision

1. `core.TrafficStore` and `core.FindingStore` are the source of truth while the process runs. Reads
   never go to SQLite.
2. `persist.Store` mirrors writes through sinks installed on the stores, and restores them on open.
   A failed mirror write is the mirror's failure, logged, not the capture's.
3. A project switch is serialised against capture by one lock taken before the stores' own mutexes
   (`core.CaptureGate`, `switch-deadlock`), and one exchange's writes are one hold (`core.CaptureHold`,
   `capture-split`), so a switch never splits an exchange across projects.
4. With `-capture-dir` message bytes live in mmap'd segments; without it they are resident.

## Consequences

- Restart correctness depends on every setting having a Save/Load pair and a restore call in
  `cmd/burpsy` (pinned by `TestSettingsWithNoTestSurviveAReopen` and `uat-cli.sh` step 6).
- The mirror still runs synchronously under the store lock (bead `store-global-lock`); resident mode
  grows the heap for the life of the process.
- Bodies are durable in two places (SQLite `messages.raw` and segments); ADR 0011 must decide which.
E
cat > 0008-committed-ui-bundle.md <<'E'
# ADR 0008 — The console bundle is committed and embedded

- **Status:** Accepted (recorded retroactively, 2026-10-27; Bead: adr-backfill)
- **Context artefacts:** `internal/web/ui/dist/`, `internal/web/ui.go` (`go:embed`), `.github/workflows/go.yml` (`ui` job, bundle freshness), `CLAUDE.md` gotchas

## Context

The Go binary serves the React console from `go:embed`. `go install` and `go build` from a checkout must
produce a working console without a JavaScript toolchain.

## Decision

1. `dist/app.js` and `dist/style.css` are committed.
2. Only the lead rebuilds them, once per round, with the pinned bun (1.4.2); implementing agents never
   commit them.
3. CI rebuilds and fails when the committed bundle differs (`ui` job, bundle freshness).

## Consequences

- Every UI change round carries one bundle commit (~2.7 MB file; 34 of the visible commits touch it).
- A stale bundle cannot merge, and a Go-only contributor never needs bun.
- Alternative rejected: build in CI and release only, embedding a stub otherwise — it breaks `go install`.
E
cat > 0009-json-rpc-plugins-exact-protocol.md <<'E'
# ADR 0009 — Extensions are JSON-RPC child processes with an exact protocol version

- **Status:** Accepted (recorded retroactively, 2026-10-27; Bead: adr-backfill)
- **Context artefacts:** `internal/extension/protocol.go` (`ProtocolVersion = 1`), `internal/extension/host.go`, `-plugins` allowlist, route class `riskExecute`

## Context

Burp's extensions run in-process with the tool's privileges. burpsy needs extensions without a plugin
ABI, without loading foreign code into the proxy's process, and without an API surface that lets a
caller start arbitrary binaries.

## Decision

1. An extension is a child process speaking JSON-RPC over stdio; `internal/extension` imports no other
   package of this module.
2. The host announces `ProtocolVersion` in `initialize` and requires an exact match: a mismatched
   extension is refused, not adapted.
3. Only binaries named in the `-plugins` allowlist can be started; the API names an allowlist key,
   never a path. Starting one is `riskExecute`, which is outside the confirmation set because the
   operator authorised the binary on the command line (pinned by
   `TestRiskExecuteIsExcludedFromTheConfirmationSetWithItsReason`).

## Consequences

- A protocol change is a version bump that every extension must follow; there is no negotiation.
- A crashing extension cannot take the proxy down with it.
E
cat > 0010-mcp-is-an-http-client-of-the-console.md <<'E'
# ADR 0010 — MCP is an HTTP client of the console, its tools derived from the route manifest

- **Status:** Accepted (recorded retroactively, 2026-10-27; Bead: adr-backfill)
- **Context artefacts:** `internal/mcp`, `cmd/burpsy-mcp`, `internal/web/route_manifest.go`, `internal/mcp/groups.go`, `burpsy-go/docs/MCP.md`

## Context

An agent driving burpsy must be held to the same scope, confirmation and audit rules as the console.
A second implementation of those rules for MCP would drift from the first.

## Decision

1. `burpsy-mcp` forwards every tool call over HTTP to a running console; it holds no state and makes no
   decision the console does not also make.
2. Its tools are generated from the route manifest; every manifest route is in exactly one MCP group or
   explicitly `notExposed`.
3. Confirmation-worthy routes need the console's one-time, call-bound token (`burpsy_confirm`).

## Consequences

- `internal/mcp` imports `internal/web` for the manifest only, so the thin client links the whole
  console (a known layering violation, bead `route-statements`: move the manifest to a leaf package).
- MCP cannot do anything the console's HTTP API refuses.
E
cat > 0011-persistence-compatibility-policy.md <<'E'
# ADR 0011 — Persistence compatibility: user_version is the only mechanism

- **Status:** Proposed (needs the owner's decision; Bead: persistence-compat-policy, adr-backfill)
- **Context artefacts:** `internal/persist/migrate.go`, `persist.go` `SaveScope` (scope_rules v3/v2/legacy), the 27 JSON settings blobs, `scanconfig-persist-format` (8edc098)

## Context

Two strategies coexist. `migrate.go` has one step and refuses a database newer than the build. Schema
changes have instead been made by writing parallel tables (`scope_rules_v3`, `_v2`, legacy) on every save
so older builds can still read them. Twenty-seven settings are unversioned JSON blobs; one of them
(`scanconfig.overrides`, Go field names, decoded onto a zero struct) silently turned new default-on
scan switches off.

## Proposal

1. SQLite `user_version` is the only compatibility mechanism. Opening is forward-only: a build refuses a
   newer file, and migrates an older one after copying it to `<db>.bak-v<N>`.
2. No more parallel `_vN` tables. The first real migration step drops the `_v2`/legacy scope writes.
3. Every JSON blob carries `{"v": N}` and is decoded onto the current defaults, so an absent key keeps its
   default (the rule 8edc098 applied to the scan configuration).
4. Decide which store is durable for message bodies (SQLite or the segment log) and stop writing both.

## Consequences if accepted

- Downgrading a project file needs the `.bak` copy, not the old build.
- Each schema change is one reviewed migration step with a reopen test.
E

class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def _go(self):
        body = f"TARGET-OK {self.command} {self.path}".encode()
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        # A Set-Cookie with attributes, for two checks at once. The session jar has to keep the pair
        # and drop the attributes — it used to store Path and SameSite as cookies and send them back.
        # And the value varies per response, so a sequencer capture that collected the same response
        # N times cannot pass for one that sent N requests.
        self.send_header("Set-Cookie", f"E2E_SESSION=tok{next(counter):04d}; Path=/; SameSite=Lax")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)
    do_GET = do_POST = _go
    def log_message(self, *a): pass

import json,sys,urllib.request
web,ca=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]
base=f"http://127.0.0.1:{web}"
cur=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base}/api/network/settings",timeout=10))
settings=cur.get("settings",cur)
settings.setdefault("tls",{})["root_ca_path"]=ca
body=json.dumps(settings)
mint=json.dumps({"method":"PUT","url":"/api/network/settings","body":body}).encode()
tok=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(f"{base}/api/network/settings/confirm",mint,{"content-type":"application/json"}),timeout=10))["token"]
req=urllib.request.Request(f"{base}/api/network/settings",body.encode(),{"content-type":"application/json","X-Burpsy-Confirm":tok},method="PUT")
print(urllib.request.urlopen(req,timeout=10).status)
PY
)
[ "$TRUST" = 200 ] && ok "the origin's certificate was added as a trusted root (confirmed PUT)" || no "network settings PUT: '$TRUST'"
curl -s -o "$TLS_WORK/ca.crt" "http://127.0.0.1:$TLS_WEB/ca.crt"'''
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)
E

~/.cache/go-build
          key: ${{ steps.env.outputs.cache-key }}

  # The required check. Branch protection names `gate` (docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md section 11), so
  # it stays one check, never skipped (if: always()), that is green only when:
  #   - `changes` succeeded (it also holds the control-byte check), and
  #   - lint and every test shard succeeded, or — only when `changes` said code=false — they were
  #     skipped. A failed or cancelled dependency is red in every case, and so is a skip that
  #     `changes` did not ask for.
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    needs: [changes, lint, test]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: changes, lint and every test shard passed (or were legitimately skipped)
        working-directory: .
        env:
          CHANGES: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          CODE: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.code }}
          MODE: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.mode }}
          LINT: ${{ needs.lint.result }}
          TEST: ${{ needs.test.result }}
        run: |
          echo "changes: $CHANGES (code=$CODE mode=$MODE)  lint: $LINT  test shards: $TEST"
          if [ "$CHANGES" != success ]; then
            echo "::error::the Go gate is red: the changes job is $CHANGES"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$CODE" = false ]; then
            for r in "$LINT" "$TEST"; do
              if [ "$r" != skipped ] && [ "$r" != success ]; then
                echo "::error::the Go gate is red: lint=$LINT, test shards=$TEST"
                exit 1
              fi
            done
            echo "Only documentation, .beads data or benchmark scripts changed: no Go job needed to run."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [ "$LINT" != success ] || [ "$TEST" != success ]; then
            echo "::error::the Go gate is red: lint=$LINT, test shards=$TEST"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$MODE" = affected ]; then
            echo "Green on the AFFECTED test set (see each shard's summary for what did not run); the full suite runs on the push to master."
          fi

    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: .
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: ./.github/actions/burpsy-test-env
        with:

  # UAT: the browser console (bead uat2; harness by the web-ui lane under ui/e2e). Playwright drives
  # the real console against a real burpsy-go the harness builds and seeds: load, send from Repeater,
  # find the exchange. The served console is the embedded ui/dist, so it is rebuilt first with the
  # pinned bun. Chrome start-up has failed on runners before (bead 2o0c), so: Playwright's own
  # Chromium, BURPSY_UAT_NO_SANDBOX=1, a 60s launch timeout, and no retries (a retry that goes green
  # hides a flake). Trace and screenshot on failure, and JUnit, are uploaded. This is

  # specs/) runs nightly as nightly.yml's e2e-ui job.

    needs: changes

    a string no HTTP client can open ("http://<host>:<port>https://example.org/")."""

entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

content.content:
The page covers installation, but it doesn't explain how to enable Entire in a repo or how it hooks into Git. It also doesn't mention hooks, branches, or refs.

**Linux install commands**

- Stable channel:
  ```bash
  curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash
  ```
- Nightly channel:
  ```bash
  curl -fsSL https://entire.com/install.sh | bash -s -- --channel nightly
  ```
- Direct download (AMD64; replace `amd64` with `arm64` in the archive name for ARM64):
  ```bash
  download_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
  curl -fsSL https://github.com/entireio/cli/releases/latest/download/entire_linux_amd64.tar.gz \
  ```

content.text:
Entire is installed and enabled, and every check passes except the checkpoint test. That test fails because Entire only records sessions that start after its hooks are installed, and this session started before.

**Before I push anything:** Entire installed a git pre-push hook. My next `git push` would upload this session's transcripts to `Chaim12345/burpsy` as checkpoint refs. The transcripts include tool output from this whole session. Entire says its secret redaction is "best effort, not bulletproof". If the repo is public, anyone could read them. So I've stopped pushing until you decide. There are two other ways to keep checkpoints:
- `entire configure --local --skip-push-sessions` keeps them local only.
- `--checkpoint-remote github:<owner>/<private-repo>` sends them to a separate private repo.

| Step | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1. CLI | `entire version` | Was missing. I installed it from the official release tarball into `~/.local/bin` instead of piping `install.sh` into bash. It reports `Entire CLI 0.12.2`, built with go1.27.3, linux/amd64 |
| 2. Enable | `entire enable -y --agent claude-code` | "Installed 10 hooks for Claude Code", "Configured project", "Ready." |
| 3a. Status | `entire status --detailed` | `● Enabled · branch beads-batch2`, Agents: Claude Code, checkpoints sync to `origin` |
| 3b. Agents | `entire agent list` | `✓ claude-code` |
| 3c. Files | `.entire/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json` | Both exist. Entire also wrote `.entire/.gitignore`. Checkpoints are stored as git refs |
| 4. Doctor | `entire doctor` | All OK: metadata branches, git hooks, Claude Code hook config, no stuck sessions |
| 5. Checkpoint | committed the setup files (907c696), then `entire checkpoint list` | `checkpoints 0`, and no link prompt appeared |

**Hooks:** each new hook in `.claude/settings.json` does nothing on a machine without `entire` installed, and the existing `bd prime` start hook is kept. I committed the three setup files on `beads-batch2`, but haven't pushed.

**To finish the checkpoint test:** start a new session, make a small change, and commit. That commit should ask to link to the session and produce a checkpoint. `entire import claude-code` can also bring in up to 30 days of past transcripts, but those get pushed the same way.

`entire enable` also mentioned that Vercel was detected. Running `entire configure` interactively stops Vercel deploying the `entire/**` branches.

My unfinished scope fix is still uncommitted. `POST /api/protobuf/reflect-decode` dials an out-of-scope host unless "drop out-of-scope" is on, unlike Repeater, which always refuses. I found it with a new egress-matrix test, which is also uncommitted. Both are on hold until you've chosen how checkpoints should be pushed. After that I'll go back to feature work, with fewer tests and short comments only where the code isn't self-explanatory.

content.text:
I committed the gRPC reflection scope fix locally on `beads-batch2` as ef4ea0b, but haven't pushed it. Its tests pass, and the working tree is now clean.

**The fix:** `POST /api/protobuf/reflect-decode` would connect to any host named in the request unless "drop out-of-scope" was on. It now refuses out-of-scope targets, the same way Repeater does. I cut its comment down to one line, as you asked.

**What found it:** a new test sends every egress and attack route at a target the scope excludes, and expects zero connections. With the target in scope instead, the same routes make 16 connections, so the test does reach the sends.

**Why nothing is pushed:** `beads-batch2` is 2 commits ahead of GitHub: the Entire setup (907c696) and this fix. Entire's pre-push hook would upload this session's transcripts to `Chaim12345/burpsy`, and its secret redaction is best-effort. Tell me which you want:
- **Push as is:** the transcripts go to the repo along with the commits.
- **Local only:** I run `entire configure --local --skip-push-sessions`, so checkpoints stay on this machine, then push.
- **Separate private repo:** I run `entire configure --local --checkpoint-remote github:<owner>/<repo>` with a repo you name, then push.

# Project Instructions for AI Agents

This file provides instructions and context for AI coding agents working on this project.

## Beads Issue Tracker

This project uses **bd (beads)** for issue tracking. Run `bd prime` to see full workflow context and commands.

### Quick Reference

```bash
bd ready              # Find available work
bd show <id>          # View issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim work
bd close <id>         # Complete work
```

### Rules

- Use `bd` for ALL task tracking — do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown TODO lists
- Run `bd prime` for detailed command reference and session close protocol
- Use `bd remember` for persistent knowledge — do NOT use MEMORY.md files

**Architecture in one line:** issues live in a local Dolt DB; sync uses `refs/dolt/data` on your git remote; `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a passive export. See https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/blob/main/docs/SYNC_CONCEPTS.md for details and anti-patterns.

## Agent Context Profiles

The managed Beads block is task-tracking guidance, not permission to override repository, user, or orchestrator instructions.

- **Conservative (default)**: Use `bd` for task tracking. Do not run git commits, git pushes, or Dolt remote sync unless explicitly asked. At handoff, report changed files, validation, and suggested next commands.
- **Minimal**: Keep tool instruction files as pointers to `bd prime`; use the same conservative git policy unless active instructions say otherwise.
- **Team-maintainer**: Only when the repository explicitly opts in, agents may close beads, run quality gates, commit, and push as part of session close. A current "do not commit" or "do not push" instruction still wins.

## Session Completion

This protocol applies when ending a Beads implementation workflow. It is subordinate to explicit user, repository, and orchestrator instructions.

1. **File issues for remaining work** - Create beads for anything that needs follow-up
2. **Run quality gates** (if code changed) - Tests, linters, builds
3. **Update issue status** - Close finished work, update in-progress items
4. **Handle git/sync by active profile**:
   ```bash
   # Conservative/minimal/default: report status and proposed commands; wait for approval.
   git status

   # Team-maintainer opt-in only, unless current instructions forbid it:
   git pull --rebase
   git push
   git status
   ```
5. **Hand off** - Summarize changes, validation, issue status, and any blocked sync/commit/push step

**Critical rules:**
- Explicit user or orchestrator instructions override this Beads block.
- Do not commit or push without clear authority from the active profile or the current user request.
- If a required sync or push is blocked, stop and report the exact command and error.
**Active profile for this repository: Conservative.** No agent commits, pushes or runs a Dolt
remote sync unless the current request says to; the lead's round workflow is
`docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md`, which wins over older instructions. Two statements in the managed
block above are wrong here and are overridden: `.beads/issues.jsonl` on master is the source of
truth, not a passive export, and `refs/dolt/data` has been dead since 2026-09-17 — never
`bd dolt push`.


## Build & Test

The active tree is `burpsy-go/` (Go module + React console under `internal/web/ui/`); `crates/` is
the frozen Rust reference (`verify.sh`). Full rules: `docs/DEVELOPMENT-PROCESS.md` section 4 and
`AGENTS.md`. Run `scripts/dev-setup.sh` once per clone.

| Tier | Who / when | What runs | Where it is defined |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | implementing agent, before reporting | `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -count=1 -timeout 30m` on `scripts/affected-go-tests.sh origin/master`; `bun run check` if the UI changed; a negative control per new test | local |
| T2 | lead, per item merge into the round branch | T1 on the merge result, plus `go build ./...` | local |
| T3 | CI, every PR into master and every master push | `gate`: gofmt, build, vet; `go test ./... -count=1` + `go test -race` on `internal/web/` and race-core (`proxy`, `dash`, `pool`, `sender`, `intruder`) — full on a master push, the affected set on a PR (full if it touches go.mod/go.sum, `.github/**`, `scripts/ci-*`, testdata); `ui`: `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, `bun run check`, `bun run build`, bundle freshness; `beads`; `review-gate`; `uat-cli` + `uat-ui` (part of `gate`). Docs/.beads/bench-only changes skip Go and ui | `.github/workflows/go.yml`, `review-gate.yml` |
| Nightly | CI, 03:17 UTC | `e2e-go.sh`; the Playwright console suite (`ui/e2e/specs`, job `e2e-ui`); every shard but `race-web-*` and `race-core` under `-race` (scanner and extscan included); `fuzz` (all targets, `ci-fuzz.sh`); `bench-vulnapp`, `bench-parity` | `.github/workflows/nightly.yml` |
| Manual | whoever changed the console | live browser pass: `./ui-live.sh` + `burpsy-go/docs/UI-VERIFICATION.md` | not in CI |

```bash
pkgs=$(scripts/affected-go-tests.sh origin/master)                  # T1 test set
[ -n "$pkgs" ] && scripts/capped-run.sh -- sh -c "cd burpsy-go && go test -count=1 -timeout 30m $pkgs"
scripts/capped-run.sh -- scripts/ci-shard.sh rest                  # one CI shard; `ci-shard.sh all` lists them
scripts/capped-run.sh -- sh -c 'cd burpsy-go && go test ./... -count=1 -timeout 30m'  # whole suite: a diagnostic
(cd burpsy-go/internal/web/ui && bun run check && bun run build)    # tsc + guards; build does NOT type-check
```

Gotchas: `go test ./...` needs `-timeout 30m` (`internal/scanner` alone is ~8 minutes); `bun run
build` strips types without checking them; agents never commit `dist/app.js` / `style.css` — the
lead rebuilds once per round with bun 1.4.2. A browser-driving package (domexec, dominvader,
blindxss, browser, crawler, scanner, web) FAILS when Chrome cannot launch; `BURPSY_ALLOW_NO_CHROME=1`
accepts that run deliberately (siblings: `BURPSY_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_COVERAGE`, `_EXTSCAN`; list in
`AGENTS.md` Testing Requirements). CI sets none of them.

## Architecture Overview

_Add a brief overview of your project architecture_

## Conventions & Patterns

_Add your project-specific conventions here_

# Testing Strategy

Design effective testing strategies balancing coverage, speed, and maintenance.

## Testing Pyramid

```
        /  E2E  \         Few, slow, high confidence
       / Integration \     Some, medium speed
      /    Unit Tests  \   Many, fast, focused
```

## Strategy by Component Type

- **API endpoints**: Unit tests for business logic, integration tests for HTTP layer, contract tests for consumers
- **Data pipelines**: Input validation, transformation correctness, idempotency tests
- **Frontend**: Component tests, interaction tests, visual regression, accessibility
- **Infrastructure**: Smoke tests, chaos engineering, load tests

## What to Cover

Focus on: business-critical paths, error handling, edge cases, security boundaries, data integrity.

Skip: trivial getters/setters, framework code, one-off scripts.

## Output

Produce a test plan with: what to test, test type for each area, coverage targets, and example test cases. Identify gaps in existing coverage.

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.
